observations.text: Anger is very often kindled by something perceived: heard or seen, stated in the verse itself
observations.meaning: Anger is very often kindled by something perceived: heard or seen, stated in the verse itself
observations.note: October disposition: W (10.2 → 10.1: hearing feeds feeling); touches: 10.1, 10.2, 10.0 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: It can be kindled by a lie, and act on it anyway
observations.meaning: It can be kindled by a lie, and act on it anyway

observations.text: The angry one misreads the other's heart
observations.meaning: The angry one misreads the other's heart
observations.note: October disposition: W (anger reckons wrongly, like 10.3); touches: 10.3, 10.9 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Anger comes where a lifted state is checked: the heart lifted by strength (Uzziah), the merry heart (Ahasuerus), the glad heart (Haman), the heart already set (Dan 11:28)
observations.meaning: Anger comes where a lifted state is checked: the heart lifted by strength (Uzziah), the merry heart (Ahasuerus), the glad heart (Haman), the heart already set (Dan 11:28)
observations.note: October disposition: W (11 §2: the threshold pattern, now with anger); touches: 11 §2, 10.1 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Four occasions of blocked will:
observations.meaning: Four occasions of blocked will: a demand no one can meet; being thwarted or made a fool of; rebuke from a holy person; refusal by an inferior

observations.text: A rival's rise:
observations.meaning: A rival's rise: the anger reckons the rival's future ("what more can he have but the kingdom?"), watches ("eyed"), and enlarges its target
observations.note: October disposition: W (anger becomes reckoning and plot: 1Sa 18:8 → 18:25); touches: 10.3, 10.9, 11 §6 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Indignation for another
observations.meaning: Indignation for another who is wronged; it states a norm ("such a thing must not be done")

observations.text: Anger at what God has done
observations.meaning: Anger at what God has done, at his striking (Uzzah) and at his mercy (Jonah, who quotes "slow to anger" against him)

observations.text: Indignation at good done
observations.meaning: Indignation at good done, defending a norm against it

observations.text: Rage at the word
observations.meaning: Rage at the word that lowers the hearers' standing or exposes their guilt. It stops its ears
observations.note: October disposition: W (10.2: refusing to hear, now with rage); touches: 10.2, 10.4 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: The fallen face:
observations.meaning: The fallen face: anger that cannot reach its cause sinks into the body (face, bed, no food), and comes out as a death

observations.text: Someone else names it.
observations.meaning: Someone else names it. God asks Cain; Jezebel names Ahab's spirit; Elkanah names Hannah's heart. The two offers that follow are opposites: "rule over it" or "I will give you the vineyard"

observations.text: Anger has a course in time:
observations.meaning: Anger has a course in time: it turns away and is forgotten (Esau); is kept "forever" (Edom); repeats (Pro 19:19); is to end before sunset (Eph 4:26–27)
observations.note: October disposition: W; feeds NS-M3 (remembering and forgetting); touches: 10.1, 11 §4, NS-M3 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Anger lodges and is cherished
observations.meaning: Anger lodges and is cherished, and the lodging is the fool's
observations.note: October disposition: W (Ch 7 already has Ecc 7:9; add Job 36:13); touches: Ch 7, 10.1 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Held anger released as a ledger
observations.meaning: Held anger released as a ledger ("these twenty years"; "these many years"); pressure in the belly, and speech as relief

observations.text: Anger turned on oneself
observations.meaning: Anger turned on oneself: wounding the self; forbidden by Joseph

observations.text: Fretting = heating oneself
observations.meaning: Fretting = heating oneself at the wicked's success. It "tends only to evil". It is replaced by trust, committing, stillness and waiting

observations.text: Vexation suffered
observations.meaning: Vexation suffered: worn down year by year, in the eye and the body, sleepless; met by being heard; Qoheleth's vexation of knowing and working; "sorrow is better than laughter"

observations.text: Anger and grief, joined.
observations.meaning: Anger and grief, joined. Jonathan's grief is for David (1Sa 20:34). Jesus "looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart" (Mar 3:5): one object for both

observations.text: Fear and anger follow one another
observations.meaning: Fear and anger follow one another: anger at God, then fear of God (2Sa 6:8–9); fear first, then anger at a weaker target (Dan 11:30)

observations.text: Kinship stops strife or feeds it
observations.meaning: Kinship stops strife or feeds it, on the same ground ("for we are kinsmen" / "the king is our close relative")

observations.text: Anger at a brother is judged like murder; worship waits on reconciliation
observations.meaning: Anger at a brother is judged like murder; worship waits on reconciliation

observations.text: The powerful one's anger
observations.meaning: The powerful one's anger decides others' fate; those beneath plead, read it, script a reply, reach it through an intermediary

observations.text: The oppressor's wrath is shown with its end in view
observations.meaning: The oppressor's wrath is shown with its end in view: the strength that carries it breaks

observations.text: The leader's anger
observations.meaning: The leader's anger at those he leads: it flares, breaks, questions, and yields to a reason

observations.text: Anger is learned from company
observations.meaning: Anger is learned from company, and the self is what is snared
observations.note: October disposition: W (11 §6: inner states pass between people); touches: 10.9, 11 §6 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: How strife is kindled and quenched
observations.meaning: How strife is kindled and quenched: fuel, pressure ("pressing anger produces strife"), a whisperer, wine, the lot

observations.text: Turning another's anger away
observations.meaning: Turning another's anger away: a soft answer, patience, a soft tongue, a gift (reported, not approved)

observations.text: The quarrelsome house
observations.meaning: The quarrelsome house: dripping, not a storm; the one who bears it withdraws

observations.text: Strife among believers is traced to an inner source
observations.meaning: Strife among believers is traced to an inner source: passions at war within, the flesh, conceit, appetite, envy behind preaching

observations.text: Anger in the lists
observations.meaning: Anger in the lists: its constant neighbours are envy, jealousy and speech-sins. It is set straight after "do not grieve the Holy Spirit"

observations.text: The enemy's anger as the one attacked bears it
observations.meaning: The enemy's anger as the one attacked bears it: swallowing, grudge, venom in speech; felt as "my heart is in anguish within me" (Psa 55:4); answered by calling on God

observations.text: Fear of another's anger, and freedom from it
observations.meaning: Fear of another's anger, and freedom from it: forgetting God feeds it; seeing the invisible frees from it

observations.text: Anger poured as a drink
observations.meaning: Anger poured as a drink to shame another, and the cup comes back
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.0 (what comes back), 10.9 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Human anger does not produce God's righteousness
observations.meaning: Human anger does not produce God's righteousness; slowness opens the way to receiving the word

observations.text: "Be angry and do not sin"
observations.meaning: "Be angry and do not sin": anger itself is not forbidden; leaving it overnight opens a door to the devil

observations.text: Love is not irritable
observations.meaning: Love is not irritable: it does not get provoked

observations.text: Human anger related to God's in four ways:
observations.meaning: Human anger related to God's in four ways: given with the Spirit (Saul, ending in mercy that day); shared as God's jealousy (Phinehas, "counted to him as righteousness"); exceeding the commission ("a rage that has reached up to heaven"); used ("the wrath of man shall praise you")

observations.text: The prophet as vessel
observations.meaning: The prophet as vessel: God's anger in a human comes out as suffering, not violence: weariness, isolation, bitterness, seven days overwhelmed

observations.text: Who may pronounce anger
observations.meaning: Who may pronounce anger: a curse cannot go beyond God's ("How can I curse whom God has not cursed?"); the same verb is valid when it follows justice

observations.text: Jesus's anger
observations.meaning: Jesus's anger: it looks, grieves and heals. Their silence becomes a plot

observations.text: Provoking and indignation turned to good
observations.meaning: Provoking and indignation turned to good: stirring one another to love; indignation as the fruit of godly grief

observations.text: The answer to human anger is most often a question or a reframing, not a rebuke
observations.meaning: The answer to human anger is most often a question or a reframing, not a rebuke: God's question to Cain and to Jonah; Joseph's "not you … but God"; the father's "this your brother"; Jesus redefining greatness and the norm; Nathan's parable

observations.text: Answered by turning to God instead
observations.meaning: Answered by turning to God instead: be still and wait; ponder on your bed and be silent; leave it to the wrath of God and feed the enemy

observations.text: Human anger is often shown with no inner word at all.
observations.meaning: Human anger is often shown with no inner word at all. It is carried by the act, the face and body, speech, another person naming it, "to themselves", a word that holds the seat inside it (aph = nostril), or the frame of a list
observations.note: October disposition: RS (Ch 14 "Beyond the named words" gains this); touches: Ch 14 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Narrative shows anger by its act; wisdom places it in the heart or spirit
observations.meaning: Narrative shows anger by its act; wisdom places it in the heart or spirit, where it can be governed or judged
observations.note: October disposition: W (as a reading); touches: Ch 14, 11 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Provoking God, and its named inner roots
observations.meaning: Provoking God, and its named inner roots: forgetting; fullness ("grew fat, and kicked"); a deceived or turning heart; false security ("I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart"); distress that drives further away (Ahaz); not believing; never satisfied
observations.note: October disposition: NS-M2 / W (12); touches: 12, NS-M2 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: The provocation turns on the provoker
observations.meaning: The provocation turns on the provoker: "Is it I whom they provoke? … Is it not themselves, to their own shame?"; they "became false"
observations.note: October disposition: W; touches: 10.0 (what comes back), 12 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Provocation handed on
observations.meaning: Provocation handed on: "made Israel to sin"; "like mother, like daughter"; the leader's failure leaves the people without a shepherd

observations.text: Asking once more, aware of the anger
observations.meaning: Asking once more, aware of the anger: boldness and restraint in one sentence; the anger feared never comes

observations.text: Intercession: standing in the breach
observations.meaning: Intercession: standing in the breach; driven by the intercessor's own fear; answered (Moses), forbidden (Jer 7:16), sought and not found (Eze 22:30), refused (Eze 9:8), insufficient (Eze 14:20), turned to imprecation (Jer 18:20–23); and the one explained by God's anger prays for the explainers (Job 42:8)

observations.text: "Slow to anger" received and used eight ways
observations.meaning: "Slow to anger" received and used eight ways: worship, plea, confession, complaint (Jonah), praise, wonder, judgement (Nahum), ground for returning (Joel). One creed; its character changes with the one who uses it
observations.note: October disposition: W (11 §4 change of character); touches: 10.8, 11 §4 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: The heart that turns, and so turns the anger
observations.meaning: The heart that turns, and so turns the anger: Josiah's tender heart; Rehoboam; Hezekiah humbled "for the pride of his heart"; partial humbling (Rehoboam "did not set his heart")
observations.note: October disposition: NS-M2 / W (13); touches: 13, NS-M2 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: The heart that does not take the blow in
observations.meaning: The heart that does not take the blow in, and the heart made "diamond-hard lest they should hear"
observations.note: October disposition: W (12 hardening; Rom 2:5 is already there); touches: 12 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Reading the ruin
observations.meaning: Reading the ruin: "Why?"; reading it rightly is the first step back; reading it as God's absence; seeing it and not turning; understood only afterwards ("In the latter days you will understand")

observations.text: Knowledge through the anger
observations.meaning: Knowledge through the anger: "they shall know that I am the Lord"; for knowledge of his rule, his purpose, his name

observations.text: Asking for the measure
observations.meaning: Asking for the measure: "Correct me, O Lord, but in justice; not in your anger"; the bearer names his own sin or limits

observations.text: Fear of being cast off, answered by remembering
observations.meaning: Fear of being cast off, answered by remembering
observations.note: October disposition: W; feeds NS-M3; touches: 10.8, NS-M3 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: "For a moment"
observations.meaning: "For a moment": the anger that passes, measured by what follows it ("joy comes with the morning"); "I will not be angry with you"

observations.text: Community lament
observations.meaning: Community lament: why? how long? restore us. The anger is felt as reaching even prayer, and as taking away the will to pray

observations.text: Zion's lament from inside
observations.meaning: Zion's lament from inside: body, hunger, the heart poured out, hope in the middle ("he does not afflict from his heart"), and an unfinished question at the end

observations.text: Bearing God's anger without knowing why
observations.meaning: Bearing God's anger without knowing why (Job; Psalm 88, which has no turn)

observations.text: Bearing it willingly because of one's sin
observations.meaning: Bearing it willingly because of one's sin, expecting the same God to plead one's cause

observations.text: Mortal life lived under the wrath; considering it is the way to a heart of wisdom
observations.meaning: Mortal life lived under the wrath; considering it is the way to a heart of wisdom

observations.text: Who can stand?
observations.meaning: Who can stand?: awe, and refuge in the same God

observations.text: Shelter while it passes
observations.meaning: Shelter while it passes: God tells his people to hide (Isa 26:20), as Job asked (Job 14:13). The reverse is to ask the mountains to hide one from God (Rev 6:16)

observations.text: False peace
observations.meaning: False peace: "surely his anger has turned from me"; "It shall be well with you"; "We have Abraham as our father"; "Let no one deceive you with empty words"

observations.text: "Who knows?"
observations.meaning: "Who knows?": returning without a guarantee

observations.text: God gives the words to return with
observations.meaning: God gives the words to return with, and the anger turns

observations.text: "Rend your hearts and not your garments"
observations.meaning: "Rend your hearts and not your garments": outward signs are not refused, but the heart is what must be torn; circumcise the heart; "did not return to me with her whole heart, but in pretense"

observations.text: The agent of wrath with a heart of its own
observations.meaning: The agent of wrath with a heart of its own goes beyond the measure and is judged; the appointed agent; the agent who did not carry it out
observations.note: October disposition: W (11 §1: acted upon, yet with its own purpose; Isa 10:7 is already in 10.6); touches: 10.6, 11 §1 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: One sins, all bear
observations.meaning: One sins, all bear; the one who sinned asks to bear it alone

observations.text: Near the holy
observations.meaning: Near the holy: the priest's grief withheld lest wrath come; David's anger, then fear, then resolved by watching another household live with the ark

observations.text: Mourning commanded
observations.meaning: Mourning commanded because the wrath has come; mourning forbidden lest it come
observations.note: October disposition: W (change of character: mourning); touches: 10.1, 11 §4 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: What the people asked for is answered in anger
observations.meaning: What the people asked for is answered in anger: a king given in anger; craving granted; "Let us be like the nations" refused

observations.text: Restraint, and the reasons God gives
observations.meaning: Restraint, and the reasons God gives: they are flesh; the spirit would faint; for my name's sake; "I am God and not a man". Two of the reasons are about what the human is

observations.text: Kindness meant to lead to repentance; wrath stored up by a hard heart
observations.meaning: Kindness meant to lead to repentance; wrath stored up by a hard heart
observations.note: October disposition: W (Rom 2:5 is in 12); touches: 12, 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Delivered from the wrath to come
observations.meaning: Delivered from the wrath to come: the response is waiting, soberness and encouraging one another, not fear

observations.text: Vengeance renounced and left to God's wrath
observations.meaning: Vengeance renounced and left to God's wrath; the enemy fed

observations.text: Put off what the wrath comes on
observations.meaning: Put off what the wrath comes on, including one's own anger (Col 3:6 then 3:8)

observations.text: The clay pleads with the potter (Isaiah); the clay is told not to answer back (Romans)
observations.meaning: The clay pleads with the potter (Isaiah); the clay is told not to answer back (Romans)
observations.note: October disposition: W (11 §1: the potter image already there via yēṣer); touches: 10.8, 11 §1 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Injustice draws the wrath as surely as idols do
observations.meaning: Injustice draws the wrath as surely as idols do; God's anger is for the widow, the orphan and the debtor who cry

observations.text: The wilderness provocation is to be remembered
observations.meaning: The wilderness provocation is to be remembered, as a cure for the heart's claim to righteousness ("Do not say in your heart … 'because of my righteousness'"), and made a daily warning ("exhort one another every day")
observations.note: October disposition: W; feeds NS-M3; touches: 10.0 (already has Deu 9:4), NS-M3 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: Meribah's inner seat is named only in the psalm's retelling: a hardened heart.
observations.meaning: Meribah's inner seat is named only in the psalm's retelling: a hardened heart. The same place is read as God's test, and Levi passed it

observations.text: No text hardens God's own heart.
observations.meaning: No text hardens God's own heart. Hardness is said of his hand, arm and sword, never his heart. The root that makes Pharaoh's heart heavy makes God glorious
observations.note: October disposition: W (11 §1 already says "I have found no text in which God hardens his own heart"); touches: 11 §1, 11 §8 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: The hand does not change; the person's position before it does
observations.meaning: The hand does not change; the person's position before it does: "strong hand" toward Egypt, toward Israel, and then against Israel
observations.note: October disposition: W (change of character: position); touches: 11 §4 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-strand-observation-ledger-v1-20261001.md)

observations.text: The narrative formula names a cause and an act.
observations.chain: broke the covenant → anger → giving over (Judg 2:14, 20)
observations.parties: God; the people; plunderers, a foreign king, fire, plague
observations.setting: Judges, Numbers, Deuteronomy narrative and covenant warning.
observations.meaning: in each of these verses the anger stands between a named act of the people and a named act of God.
observations.implication: the narrator does not leave the anger unexplained in these verses; the cause is stated in the same verse or the one before (U2 §7, §8, §16).

observations.text: One man's act, the whole people bear it.
observations.chain: one man took → the people broke faith → anger
observations.parties: Achan; the people; God
observations.setting: Jericho's devoted things (Jos 6–7).
observations.meaning: the verse calls Achan's theft the people's breach.
observations.implication: the anger is reckoned to the people for one member's act; it turns only when the act is dealt with (AG-42).

observations.text: The anger is kindled on hearing.
observations.chain: heard → anger → fire (Num 11:1)
observations.parties: the people (speakers); God (hearer)
observations.meaning: the verses state the same order for God as for people (AG-44): something heard, then the anger, then an act.
observations.implication: I read the complaint "in the hearing of the Lord" as speech that God is shown to hear; the anger answers words.

observations.text: Anger and jealousy named together.
observations.chain: other gods → jealousy and anger (Deu 6:14–15)
observations.parties: God; the people; other gods
observations.setting: Deu 6 and 29: the turn to other gods.
observations.meaning: jealousy is named beside the anger in the setting of other gods and broken covenant.
observations.implication: the anger in these verses guards an exclusive bond. Pro 27:4 sets jealousy beyond human anger ("who can stand before jealousy?", AG-53). The two statements are not joined by any verse.

observations.text: The created world bears the anger with the people.
observations.chain: anger → heavens shut → no fruit (Deu 11:17)
observations.parties: God; the land, beasts, trees, mountains; the people
observations.meaning: land, beasts, trees, rain and mountains are named as bearing the anger.
observations.implication: the physical world is a party in its own right in these verses (ruling 6.2), not a picture. The Sheol line is death-side.
observations.note: October disposition: W; Sheol H (OT-08); also appears: 13, Ch 2 (Sheol) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit1-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The anger pictured as fire, smoke and breath.
observations.parties: God
observations.meaning: the anger is described by heat, smoke, breath, lips and tongue. Job 4:9 (Eliphaz) sets "breath" beside "the blast of his anger".
observations.implication: the word itself is the nostril (§L.1, AN), and these verses keep the breath and the mouth in view. I read this as the word's own picture, not a doctrine of God's body.

observations.text: The anger spends itself, and what follows.
observations.chain: anger spent → "they shall know that I am the Lord" (Eze 5:13)
observations.parties: God; Jerusalem
observations.setting: Ezekiel's sign against Jerusalem (Eze 5).
observations.meaning: the anger is described as having a measure that is used up; Eze 5:13 then names knowledge as the outcome.
observations.implication: the anger in Eze 5:13 has an end within itself, and its end is that "they shall know".

observations.text: Struck, and not taken to heart.
observations.chain: anger poured → not understood, not taken to heart
observations.parties: God; Jacob/Israel
observations.setting: Isa 42:24: "Who gave up Jacob to the looter …? Was it not the Lord, against whom we have sinned".
observations.meaning: the anger is felt in full and not understood.
observations.implication: suffering under the anger does not by itself bring understanding; Jer 23:20 places understanding "in the latter days" (AG-29).
observations.note: October disposition: D; also appears: 04 (heart: D), 13 (D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit1-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: A king given and taken in anger; a census incited.
observations.chain: anger → incited David (2Sa 24:1)
observations.parties: God; Israel; the king
observations.setting: Hos 13:10: "Give me a king and princes".
observations.meaning: in Hos 13:11 the anger acts by granting what was asked; in 2Sa 24:1 it acts through the king's own deed.
observations.implication: I set the two side by side; no verse joins them. U2 §18, §51.
observations.note: October disposition: W; also appears: 10.6 (Hos 13:11: D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit1-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Too near the holy.
observations.chain: defiled by nearness → consumed
observations.parties: God; the kings of Israel
observations.meaning: the kings built against the temple; nearness without holiness is named as the cause.
observations.implication: with Uzzah (AG-14), the anger meets what touches the holy wrongly (U2 §6).

observations.text: The provocation remembered, and added to by a new generation.
observations.parties: Moses (speaker); the fathers; the sons
observations.setting: Moses recalls Horeb (Deu 9:7–8); Moses to Reuben and Gad (Num 32); Psa 95 read to a later generation.
observations.meaning: the anger is told again to the next generation as a warning.
observations.implication: remembering the anger is a commanded act (Deu 9:7, "Remember"); the anger has a history the hearers stand inside.

observations.text: Moses: anger, and Aaron provided in the same breath.
observations.chain: refusal → anger → Aaron given
observations.parties: God; Moses; Aaron
observations.setting: Exo 4:13: "Oh, my Lord, please send someone else."
observations.meaning: the anger answers the refusal, and the same speech gives Moses a helper.
observations.implication: the anger here does not withdraw the call; it comes with provision.

observations.text: Moses names the people as the reason.
observations.chain: "because of you" → anger → not to enter
observations.parties: Moses; the people; God
observations.meaning: Moses states that the anger came to him "on your account".
observations.implication: I keep it as Moses' own account; the cause given elsewhere (Num 20:12) is not in this unit.

observations.text: Uzzah: two accounts, two named causes.
observations.chain: hand put out to the ark → anger → struck
observations.parties: God; Uzzah; the ark
observations.meaning: Samuel names "his error"; Chronicles names the hand put out.
observations.implication: the act was with the hand (OT-06). The death side is held.
observations.note: October disposition: W; death H (OT-08); also appears: 13 (2Sa 6:7: D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit1-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Two angers on one road: God's at Balaam, Balaam's at the donkey.
observations.chain: God's anger → angel in the way → donkey lies down → Balaam's anger → strikes
observations.parties: God; the angel; Balaam; the donkey
observations.meaning: God's anger stands in the way unseen by the man; the animal sees it; the man's anger falls on the animal.
observations.implication: the man angry at what blocks him does not see what is actually blocking him (U2 §11, U1 §4).

observations.text: Wrath with no pity and no hearing.
observations.parties: God; Jerusalem's elders
observations.setting: Eze 8, the abominations in the temple.
observations.meaning: the wrath is stated with three refusals: not sparing, not pitying, not hearing.
observations.implication: in unit 1 the anger was kindled by hearing (AG-03); here the cry is heard and not answered. I set the two side by side; no verse joins them.

observations.text: Fury and discipline, joined and separated.
observations.chain: sins → fury, discipline sevenfold (Lev 26:28)
observations.parties: God; Israel; David
observations.setting: Lev 26, the covenant curses; Psa 6 and 38, David's prayers.
observations.meaning: Lev 26:28 puts fury and discipline together. David asks for discipline without the wrath.
observations.implication: extends AG-35 (Jer 10:24, "Correct me … not in your anger") with the covenant text that joins what the prayer asks to separate.

observations.text: The furnace, and the cleansing refused.
observations.chain: melted → "you shall know that I am the Lord" (Eze 22:22) · not cleansed → fury until satisfied (Eze 24:13)
observations.parties: God; the house of Israel
observations.meaning: Eze 22 pictures the wrath as a smelter's fire on gathered metals, with knowing as the stated end. Eze 24:13 says God "would have cleansed" and they "were not cleansed".
observations.implication: I read the furnace as the metalworker's picture of melting and testing. The verses themselves state melting and knowing, not refining, so I do not add it. Eze 24:13 states a cleansing offered and refused before the fury.

observations.text: Told in a dirge.
observations.parties: God; the princes; the vine
observations.setting: the lament over the princes of Israel (Eze 19).
observations.meaning: the fury is told in a lament, and the chapter names itself so (19:14).
observations.implication: the wrath can be spoken as grief. The 2026-10-01 ledger noted that qînāh (lament, H7015, unit 4) is tagged in M02.
observations.note: October disposition: W; also appears: M03 (grief); unit 4 (qînāh) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Already read in unit 1:
observations.parties: as unit 1
observations.meaning: ḥēmāh adds no separate statement in these verses beyond its pairing with ʾaph. Isa 42:25 is the one place the surface "heat" stands with "anger" ("the heat of his anger").

observations.text: Wrath as a storm, on a named group.
observations.chain: whitewash → wrath spent on the wall and its plasterers (Eze 13:15)
observations.parties: God; the false prophets; the wicked
observations.setting: Eze 13 against the prophets who whitewash a flimsy wall; Jer 23:19 inside the oracle on the prophets; Jer 30:23 repeats Jer 23:19 word for word inside the book of restoration (Jer 30–31).
observations.meaning: the storm is aimed at those who covered over what was weak, and at "the wicked".
observations.implication: one sentence stands in two settings, among the false prophets and among the promises. Both are followed by the "latter days" line (Jer 23:20; 30:24, AG-29). Change of character by setting (§C).
observations.note: October disposition: W; also appears: 10.11 (whitewash, covering) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: "My wrath upheld me": God's heart named with the wrath.
observations.chain: no one to help → my own arm, my wrath upheld me (Isa 63:5)
observations.parties: God; the peoples; Edom; no helper
observations.setting: Isa 63:1–6, the one coming from Edom in red garments.
observations.meaning: the day of vengeance and the year of redemption are held together "in my heart" (63:4). God is "appalled" that no one helps, and the wrath "upheld" him.
observations.implication: this is a third place where God's heart is named in connection with his anger (with Hos 11:8 and Jer 23:20, unit 1 F.2). Here the heart holds vengeance and redemption in one sentence. "Alone" and "no one to help" make the absence of other parties part of the account (ruling 6.2). Extends AG-25 and #1890.
observations.note: October disposition: W; RS (Ch 13, OT-13); also appears: 13; #1890 findings (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Repayment, vengeance, and "keeps wrath".
observations.chain: deeds → repayment, wrath (Isa 59:18) · vengeance → "they will know that I am the Lord" (Eze 25:17)
observations.parties: God; adversaries, the nations, Philistia
observations.setting: Nah 1:2 is followed by "The Lord is slow to anger and great in power" (1:3, AG-32) and "The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble" (1:7, AN-71).
observations.meaning: the wrath is measured "according to their deeds" and directed at adversaries; Nahum "keeps" it.
observations.implication: in Nahum 1 wrath, slowness to anger and refuge stand in consecutive verses of one psalm. The verses set them side by side; I do not join them further.

observations.text: Already read or stated in unit 1:
observations.parties: God; Gog, Egypt, the nations
observations.meaning: Same face as unit 1 C. ḥēmāh adds the pouring (Nah 1:6; Eze 30:15).
observations.note: October disposition: D (Nah 1:6); W; also appears: 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Jealousy and wrath, against the people and for them.
observations.chain: adultery, blood → blood of wrath and jealousy (Eze 16:38) · reproach of the nations → jealous wrath (Eze 36:6)
observations.parties: God; Jerusalem; the nations; the land, mountains and hills
observations.setting: Eze 16 and 23, Jerusalem pictured as an unfaithful wife; Eze 36:6 addressed to "the mountains and hills" of Israel; Zec 8:2 the promise to return to Zion.
observations.meaning: the same pairing, jealousy with wrath, is turned against Jerusalem in Eze 16 and 23, and on her behalf in Eze 36 and Zec 8.
observations.implication: what decides its face is whom the bond is defended against: the unfaithful one, or those who reproached her. Extends AG-04.

observations.text: The husband's fury.
observations.chain: jealousy → furious → will not spare, no compensation (Pro 6:34–35)
observations.parties: the husband; the adulterer
observations.setting: Pro 6:20–35, the warning against adultery.
observations.meaning: jealousy "makes" a man furious, and the fury refuses any gift (contrast Pro 21:14, where a gift averts anger).
observations.implication: Eze 16:38 and Pro 6:34 both set jealous fury in the setting of adultery, one God's and one a husband's. I set them side by side; no verse joins them.
observations.note: October disposition: D; pairing W; also appears: 10.1, 11 (D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Phinehas: jealous "with my jealousy".
observations.chain: jealous with my jealousy → wrath turned back → not consumed (Num 25:11); jealous for his God → atonement (25:13)
observations.parties: Phinehas; God; Israel
observations.meaning: a man shares God's jealousy, and the wrath turns back. AN-40.

observations.text: Satisfied, and then calm.
observations.chain: wrath satisfied → jealousy departs → calm, no more angry (Eze 16:42) · not remembered → enraged (16:43)
observations.parties: God; Jerusalem
observations.setting: Eze 16:42 is followed by "Because you have not remembered the days of your youth, but have enraged me with all these things" (16:43).
observations.meaning: the wrath has an end stated within it ("satisfy", "spend"), and Eze 16:42 names what follows: jealousy departs, calm, no more anger.
observations.implication: extends AG-07 (Eze 5:13). Eze 16:43 names not remembering as a cause of the rage (10.3).

observations.text: The king's wrath abates too.
observations.chain: Haman hanged → wrath abated (Est 7:10) · anger abated → he remembered (Est 2:1)
observations.parties: Ahasuerus; Haman; Vashti
observations.meaning: a ruler's wrath also has an end, after the hanging (Est 7:10) and after time (Est 2:1). In Est 2:1 remembering comes once the anger has gone.
observations.implication: "satisfy … calm" (God, Eze 16:42) and "abated" (the king) are said in the same way of both. I set them side by side (R).
observations.note: October disposition: D (Est 2:1); W; also appears: 10.3 (Est 2:1: D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: "I said I would pour out my wrath … But I acted for the sake of my name."
observations.chain: rebelled → "I said I would pour out my wrath" → acted for my name, withheld my hand (Eze 20:8–9, 13–14, 21–22)
observations.parties: God; Israel; the nations watching
observations.setting: Eze 20 retells Israel's history in three rounds: Egypt, the first generation in the wilderness, their children.
observations.meaning: each round has rebellion, the wrath resolved on, then the wrath withheld "for the sake of my name … in the sight of the nations".
observations.implication: the stated reason for restraint is God's name before onlookers, not the people's merit. Extends AN-82 (Isa 48:9). The nations are a party to the restraint (ruling 6.2).

observations.text: Restraint for compassion, and for humbling.
observations.chain: compassionate → atoned, did not destroy, did not stir up all his wrath (Psa 78:38) · humbled → wrath not poured out (2Ch 12:7)
observations.parties: God; Rehoboam and the princes; Shemaiah; Shishak (the hand not used)
observations.meaning: two further reasons are stated: compassion (Psa 78:38, AG-28) and the people's humbling (2Ch 12:7). "Not … all his wrath" (Psa 78:38) is restraint in part; "some deliverance" (2Ch 12:7) is relief in part.
observations.implication: extends AG-45 (humbling turns the anger) with ḥēmāh's verb: "my wrath shall not be poured out".
observations.note: October disposition: D (Psa 78:38); W; also appears: 02, 11, 13 (Psa 78:38: D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: "I have no wrath."
observations.parties: God; the vineyard; thorns and briers
observations.setting: "In that day", the song of the pleasant vineyard (Isa 27:2–5), which answers the vineyard song of Isa 5.
observations.meaning: God says he has no wrath toward the vineyard he keeps. The burning is reserved for thorns and briers, and even they are invited to "make peace with me".
observations.implication: the same God who pours wrath on the vineyard elsewhere states its absence here, in the setting of keeping and peace. Change of character by time ("in that day", §C).
observations.note: October disposition: W; NS for 10.13; also appears: 13; 14 (made new) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Wrath in the act of ruling and gathering.
observations.chain: drove them in wrath → gather, bring back, dwell in safety (Jer 32:37)
observations.parties: God; Israel scattered; the peoples
observations.setting: Eze 20:33–38 goes on to "the wilderness of the peoples" where he will "enter into judgment" and purge the rebels.
observations.meaning: "a mighty hand and an outstretched arm" is the Exodus phrase (Deu 4:34, AN-95). Here "with wrath poured out" is added to it, aimed at Israel, in a new bringing out. In Jer 32:37 the wrath is what scattered them, and the gathering follows it.
observations.implication: the wrath stands inside the act of kingship and gathering, not only outside it as punishment. Change of character by position (AN-95).
observations.note: October disposition: W; also appears: 11 §4 (AN-95); OT-06 (hand) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The cup of his wrath: drunk, and taken away.
observations.chain: drunk the cup → staggering, sons fainted, "full of the wrath" (Isa 51:17, 20) · cup taken → given to the tormentors (51:22–23)
observations.parties: God; Jerusalem; her sons; her tormentors
observations.setting: Isa 51:17–23. The speaker is "your God who pleads the cause of his people" (51:22); the hearers are "afflicted, who are drunk, but not with wine" (51:21).
observations.meaning: the wrath is drunk, and the drinker staggers, faints and is "full of" it. Then the cup is taken away and passed to the tormentors who said "Bow down, that we may pass over" (51:23).
observations.implication: this is wrath taken inside the person, its effect stated in the body and the will (staggering, fainting). The cup has an end for the drinker, and passes on.
observations.note: October disposition: NS for 10.13; also appears: — (not in the chapters) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The cup handed out by the prophet, and wished on the wicked.
observations.chain: drink → stagger, crazed, because of the sword (Jer 25:16)
observations.parties: God; Jeremiah; the nations; Job; the wicked; David
observations.setting: Jer 25:15–29, the prophet as cup-bearer to the nations; Job 21:20, Job on what the wicked ought to suffer and do not (21:17, unit 1 face J); Psa 11:6, David.
observations.meaning: a man hands the cup on (Jeremiah); a man wishes it on others (Job). In Psa 11:6 zalʿāp̄āh ("scorching") is the wind in the cup.
observations.implication: the parties around the cup are named: the giver (God), the bearer (the prophet), the drinker (the nations), and the one who asks why it does not reach the wicked (Job).

observations.text: A man pours his wrath as a drink.
observations.chain: pours wrath on neighbours → the Lord's cup comes around to you (Hab 2:15–16)
observations.parties: the Chaldean; his neighbours; the Lord
observations.setting: the woes against the Chaldean (Hab 2).
observations.meaning: a man pours his own wrath into others, to shame them. The Lord's cup "will come around" to him.
observations.implication: the same picture (wrath as drink) is used for man and for God, and the man's cup is answered by God's. AN-35.
observations.note: October disposition: D; W with AG-82; also appears: 10.0 (D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: One word, rendered as wrath and as venom.
observations.parties: the wicked; serpents, asps; God; Job's spirit
observations.setting: Psa 58:3: "The wicked are estranged from the womb; they go astray from birth, speaking lies". Psa 140:3 is about the tongue and lips. Deu 32:32–33: "their vine comes from the vine of Sodom". Deu 32:24 is the covenant curse. Job 6:4 is Job's complaint.
observations.meaning: six of the 125 ḥēmāh hits are venom or poison. In the wicked it sits with lies, the stopped ear, the tongue and the lips. In Job 6:4 it is the Almighty's, and Job's spirit "drinks" it.
observations.implication: I read the word as reaching from heat to venom: what burns inside, and what poisons when it comes out. The verses do not call the venom anger; the shared word is the link, and I mark it R. Deu 32:24 is literal creatures (data).
observations.note: October disposition: W; NS (§C); also appears: 10.5 (Psa 140:3: D); 10.12, 13 (Job 6:4: D); 11 §4 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Intercession: afraid, in the breach, on his face, and reversed.
observations.chain: afraid → prayed → listened (Deu 9:19) · stood in the breach → wrath turned (Psa 106:23) · "they have dug a pit for my life" → "deliver up their children" (Jer 18:20–21)
observations.parties: Moses, Daniel, Ezekiel, Jeremiah; God; the people
observations.setting: Jer 18:20 is followed at once by "Therefore deliver up their children to famine" (18:21).
observations.meaning: Moses names his own fear of the wrath (Deu 9:19). Ezekiel's cry is a question. Jeremiah recalls his past intercession, then asks for the wrath. AG-33, AN-55.
observations.implication: fear of the wrath moves the intercessor (10.12). The same man who stood in the breach turns to imprecation within two verses.
observations.note: October disposition: D; Eze 9:8 W; also appears: 13; 10.11; 10.12 (D for Deu 9:19, Psa 106:23, Jer 18:20) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Lament: heavy, burning, dismaying, and hidden.
observations.chain: wrath heavy → companions shun (Psa 88:7–8: stated in sequence)
observations.parties: Heman; Ethan; Moses; God; companions
observations.meaning: the wrath is felt as weight (Psa 88:7), as fire with no end in view (89:46), as dismay (90:7). Psa 89:46 sets God hiding himself in the same question as the wrath burning. Psa 88:8 names the loss of companions.
observations.implication: the wrath is borne in the body's language (weight, waves) and in relationships (companions shun). Psalm 90's "our days" and "brought to an end" are death-side. AN-68, AN-70.
observations.note: October disposition: W; Psa 90 H (OT-08); also appears: 13 (Psa 90:7: D); 10.10 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Called down, after asking for it to end.
observations.chain: devoured Jacob → "Pour out your wrath on the nations" (Jer 10:25) · consumed → "that they may know that God rules" (Psa 59:13)
observations.parties: Asaph; Jeremiah; David; God; the nations
observations.meaning: in Psa 79:5–6 and Jer 10:24–25 the prayer moves, in consecutive verses, from the wrath on "us" to the wrath on the nations. Psa 59:13 states knowing as the end asked for. AG-34, AG-35, AN-62.
observations.implication: the sequence is in the text itself. I add nothing to it.

observations.text: The book heard, the wrath recognised.
observations.chain: book heard → wrath recognised → inquire (2Ki 22:13) · heart penitent, humbled → "I also have heard you" (22:19)
observations.parties: Josiah; Huldah; Jeremiah, Baruch; the people
observations.setting: Josiah, on hearing the found book read (2Ki 22; 2Ch 34); Jeremiah's scroll read by Baruch (Jer 36).
observations.meaning: the wrath is recognised by hearing the written word. Josiah's heart is answered while the wrath on the place stands (22:20).
observations.implication: the heart's penitence is heard for the king, not for the place. AG-46 (Jer 36:7, "It may be").

observations.text: Wrath as warning, and as enticement.
observations.chain: wrath → punishment of the sword → "that you may know there is a judgment" (Job 19:29) · wrath → entice into scoffing (Job 36:18: "lest")
observations.parties: Job; the friends; Elihu
observations.meaning: whose wrath it is is not stated in either verse (ledger v5 marks both B5, both sides). Job turns the friends' accusation back on them; Elihu warns that wrath may "entice" Job into scoffing.
observations.implication: I read Job 36:18 as wrath acting on a person as an enticer, drawing him into scoffing, whether it is his own or the wrath he fears. The verse does not decide which; I leave it open.

observations.text: The prophet full of it.
observations.chain: ears uncircumcised → full of the wrath, weary of holding it in (Jer 6:10–11) · heat of my spirit → overwhelmed seven days (Eze 3:14–15)
observations.parties: Jeremiah; Ezekiel; the Spirit; the hand of the Lord; the people
observations.setting: Jer 6:10: "their ears are uncircumcised, they cannot listen".
observations.meaning: God's wrath is in a man, who holds it in until he is weary (Jeremiah). The "heat" (ḥēmāh) is "of my spirit" (Ezekiel), with the Spirit and the hand of the Lord upon him, and ends in seven days overwhelmed.
observations.implication: Eze 3:14 and Job 6:4 are the two verses in this unit that set ḥēmāh with the human spirit: the prophet's heat, and the sufferer's drink. AN-41.

observations.text: Agents of the wrath, and the rage that goes past it.
observations.chain: given into your hand → killed in a rage → fierce wrath upon you (2Ch 28:9–11) · judgment committed to them → they deal with you in fury (Eze 23:24–25)
observations.parties: God; Oded; Israel's army; Judah; the lovers; Edom
observations.meaning: God's wrath given to agents, Israel's army against Judah (2Ch 28), Jerusalem's lovers (Eze 23:22–25), Israel against Edom (Eze 25:14, AG-48). Oded rebukes the agents for a rage beyond the commission, and the wrath turns onto them.
observations.implication: the agent's own rage is a separate thing from the wrath it carries, and it is judged. AN-40.
observations.note: October disposition: D; W; also appears: 10.1, 10.9 (2Ch 28:9: D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The king's wrath, burning within, showing in the face.
observations.chain: refused → enraged, burned within (Est 1:12) · filled with fury → face changed → furnace heated (Dan 3:19)
observations.parties: Ahasuerus; Vashti; Nebuchadnezzar; the three men
observations.meaning: the wrath is placed "within him" (Est 1:12). It "filled" the king, and his face changed (Dan 3:19), then came the order.
observations.implication: inside, then face, then act, is the order the verses give. In Dan 3:19 the heat of the word and the heat of the furnace meet in one verse (I read the furnace as the act that carries the fury out; the verse states only the sequence). AN-05.

observations.text: Those beneath the ruler's wrath.
observations.chain: king's wrath → "messenger of death" → the wise appease it (Pro 16:14) · king arose in wrath → Haman begged (Est 7:7)
observations.parties: Joab, the messenger, David; the wise; Ahasuerus, Haman, Esther
observations.meaning: Joab foresees David's wrath and scripts the messenger's answer (2Sa 11:20–21). The wise appease it. Haman reads it and begs.
observations.implication: those beneath act on the ruler's wrath before it is spoken. AN-24. Pro 16:14's "messenger of death" is death-side.
observations.note: October disposition: W; Pro 16:14 death side H (OT-08); also appears: 10.9; 10.10 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Alarm, then fury; a vision of power.
observations.chain: news → alarm → great fury → destroy (Dan 11:44)
observations.parties: the king of the north; the goat and the ram
observations.setting: Daniel's visions of the kings (Dan 8, 11).
observations.meaning: in Dan 11:44 alarm comes first and the fury follows.
observations.implication: fear and fury stated in sequence in one ruler (10.12; overview part F). AN-25 (the oppressor's strength breaks: Dan 8:7–8).

observations.text: Seen, and filled with fury; joy turned in a moment.
observations.chain: saw no homage → filled with fury → sought to destroy all the Jews (Est 3:5–6) · glad of heart → saw → filled with wrath (Est 5:9) · "I thought" → rage (2Ki 5:11–12)
observations.parties: Haman; Mordecai; the Jews; Naaman; Elisha; his servants
observations.meaning: Haman's fury is kindled by what he sees: a man who does not bow, rise or tremble. In Est 5:9 he passes from "joyful and glad of heart" to wrath on a single sight. Naaman's rage answers what he "thought" would happen.
observations.implication: the wrath enlarges its target (one man → "all the Jews", Est 3:6). Naaman's rage is turned by his servants (2Ki 5:13). AN-01, AN-05, AN-06.
observations.note: October disposition: D; 2Ki 5:12 W; also appears: 10.1, 10.10, 11 (D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit2-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Fearing the oppressor's wrath, having forgotten the Maker.
observations.chain: — (set together in one question)
observations.parties: God the comforter; his people; the oppressor
observations.meaning: God the comforter sets, in one question, fear of a mortal's wrath beside forgetting the Maker. He ends with "where is the wrath of the oppressor?"
observations.implication: the verse places the two together; it does not say one causes the other, and I do not add it. Fear of human wrath is answered by remembering who made the heavens.

observations.text: What ḥēmāh adds in the sayings: a person named by it.
observations.chain: hot-tempered → strife (Pro 15:18) · man of wrath → strife; given to anger → transgression (29:22) · man of great wrath → penalty; deliver him → again (19:19) · wrath → evil (Psa 37:8)
observations.parties: the hot-tempered, the man of wrath; the one who delivers; Esau, Rebekah
observations.meaning: "a man of wrath" and "a hot-tempered man" (literally a man of heat) name a person by the word. It is something to "forsake" (Psa 37:8), and it "turns away" with time (Gen 27:44). Pro 19:19 says delivering such a man must be repeated.
observations.implication: unit 1 (AG-51 to AG-53, AN-14, AN-27, AN-28) covers these sayings. ḥēmāh adds that the word can become what the person is called.

observations.text: Hot indignation that seizes.
observations.chain: the wicked forsake the law → hot indignation seizes me
observations.parties: the psalmist; the wicked; the law
observations.setting: Psalm 119, a prayer about the law.
observations.meaning: zalʿāp̄āh (scorching) seizes the psalmist; he is acted on by it. Its cause is stated: the wicked forsaking the law.
observations.implication: the heat is spoken in prayer, with its cause named. AN-07 (indignation for another).

observations.text: Man's wrath, and the remnant of wrath.
observations.parties: man; God; the humble
observations.setting: 76:9: "when God arose to establish judgment, to save all the humble of the earth".
observations.meaning: two hits, two parties: man's wrath made to praise God; and God girding himself with what remains. AN-40 (man's wrath used).

observations.text: The same heat words, with no anger.
observations.chain: heat of wine → princes sick (Hos 7:5) · hearts like an oven → anger smolders → blazes (7:6)
observations.parties: the Gibeonites; Job; the bereaved city; the princes, the king
observations.setting: Hos 7:5 is followed by "For with hearts like an oven they approach their intrigue; all night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire. All of them are hot as an oven" (7:6–7).
observations.meaning: ḥām is the warmth of bread and garments. zalʿāp̄āh is famine's heat in the skin. ḥēmāh is the heat of wine (Hos 7:5).
observations.implication: the anger words of this unit are heat words, and Hos 7:5–7 moves within three verses from wine's heat to hearts like an oven to anger blazing. That sequence is in the text. Jos 9:12 and Job 37:17 stay in the data (no inner-being content). Lam 5:10 is famine (death side).

observations.text: The burning verb, with and without ʾaph.
observations.chain: kindled → abhorred his heritage → gave them into the hand of the nations (Psa 106:40–41)
observations.parties: God; his people; Cain; Jonah
observations.meaning: ḥārāh is the verb to burn, to be kindled. With ʾaph it is the formula "the anger … was kindled" (unit 1 AG-01, 94 shared verses). Without ʾaph the ESV gives the same verb as "was angry".
observations.implication: when the ESV says Cain or Jonah "was angry", the Hebrew says the burning word of "the anger of the Lord was kindled". The heat picture of unit 2 (AG-60, AG-101) continues in the verb.

observations.text: Added to by a new generation.
observations.chain: fathers' wandering → "a brood of sinful men" → increase the fierce anger (Num 32:13–14) · profaning the Sabbath → more wrath (Neh 13:18)

observations.setting: Moses to Reuben and Gad (Num 32), after "until all the generation that had done evil … was gone" (32:13); Nehemiah confronting the nobles (Neh 13:17).
observations.meaning: the anger has a measure that a later generation can add to, with the fathers' acts named first.
observations.implication: extends AG-11 (the provocation remembered). Two speakers a thousand years apart say the same thing in their own words.

observations.text: Wrath on a whole multitude stops ordinary joy, mourning and courage.
observations.chain: wrath upon all → let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn (Eze 7:12) · wrath upon all → none goes to battle (7:14)
observations.parties: God; the buyer, the seller; the army
observations.setting: Ezekiel 7: "An end has come; the end has come" (Eze 7:6).
observations.meaning: the buyer's gladness and the seller's grief are both set aside, and the trumpet sounds and no one moves.
observations.implication: the verses state the wrath as the reason ordinary movements of joy, sorrow and courage come to nothing.

observations.text: Toil for nothing, and shame.

observations.parties: God; Judah; the land
observations.meaning: the fierce anger is named as the reason the work of their hands comes to nothing, and as the reason for their shame.

observations.text: The fierce anger is the anger spoken of as turning.

observations.text: "Made Israel to sin": a leader's provocation carries the people.
observations.chain: made Israel to sin → the anger he provoked → the house cut off (1Ki 15:29–30)
observations.parties: Jeroboam, Baasha, Elah, Omri, Ahab, Ahaziah; Israel; Jehu the prophet; Josiah
observations.meaning: in five verses of Kings the provoking king is the one who "made Israel to sin". The provocation has a measure ("more … than all the kings"). Baasha is judged both for being like Jeroboam and for destroying his house. Josiah removes what earlier kings made to provoke.
observations.implication: Ch 13 has It is handed on (1Ki 14:16). In 1Ki 16:7 Baasha is judged for destroying a house that had already been condemned (1Ki 14:10); compare the agent who exceeds (AG-92). I set the two side by side (R).
observations.note: October disposition: D; W; also appears: 13 (handed on: D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Indignation, and what each one does with it.
observations.chain: outrageous thing → indignant, very angry → answered deceitfully (Gen 34:7, 13) · heard → very angry; hated → spoke neither good nor bad (2Sa 13:21–22) · heard the outcry → very angry → took counsel with myself → brought charges (Neh 5:6–7)
observations.parties: the sons of Jacob, Shechem, Dinah; David, Absalom, Amnon, Tamar; Nehemiah, the nobles, the poor
observations.meaning: each anger is for a wrong done to another (Dinah, Tamar, the poor under interest), and each verse or the next says what follows. The sons of Jacob answer "deceitfully" (Gen 34:13). David's anger is stated with no act, and Absalom's hatred is stated as silence, until he has Amnon killed (2Sa 13:28). Nehemiah "took counsel with myself" before acting.
observations.implication: the same indignation goes three ways: deceit and slaughter, nothing done, counsel then open charge. Jacob's verdict on his sons' anger is Gen 49:6–7 (AG-53). Extends AG-55.
