observations.chain: angry, face fallen → "Why?" → do well / sin at the door, rule over it (Gen 4:6–7) → killed Abel (4:8) · angry for the plant → "angry enough to die" → "should not I pity Nineveh?" (Jon 4:9–11)
observations.parties: God; Cain, Abel; Jonah; Nineveh; the plant
observations.meaning: in both accounts God answers a man's anger with questions, and both use "do well". To Cain he adds the warning: sin at the door, its desire for him, and "you must rule over it". Cain answers with murder (Gen 4:8). Jonah answers "angry enough to die", and the book ends on God's question about pity (4:10–11).
observations.implication: these are the two places in this unit where God speaks to an angry man about his anger, and he does it by asking. I set them side by side (R); each is in the chapters separately.
observations.note: October disposition: D; NS for 10.13 (the pairing); also appears: 10.0, 10.9, 11, 15 (Gen 4:6: D); 02, 10.1 (Jon 4:9: D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Angry with oneself, released by naming God's purpose.
observations.chain: sold me → angry with yourselves → do not, for God sent me (Gen 45:5)
observations.parties: Joseph; his brothers; God
observations.meaning: the anger is turned inward, at what they did. Joseph names God's purpose as the reason not to keep it.
observations.implication: already in 10.1 (D). The reason given is God's sending, not their innocence.

observations.text: "Fret not yourself": the burning verb turned on oneself.
observations.chain: fret → tends only to evil (Psa 37:8) · fret, envy → "the evil man has no future" (Pro 24:19–20)
observations.parties: the one addressed; evildoers; the Lord
observations.meaning: the reflexive form of ḥārāh: to heat oneself (10.1 already says so). All four are about evildoers or the one who prospers; two set it beside envy (Psa 37:1; Pro 24:19).
observations.implication: the reason given is what the evildoer's end is (Pro 24:20) and what the fretting does: "it tends only to evil" (Psa 37:8). Psa 37 sets trust, commit, be still in its place (37:3, 5, 7).
observations.note: October disposition: D; also appears: 10.1 (Psa 37:8: D); 10.9, 14 (Psa 37:7: D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The rival's provocation becomes Hannah's vexation.
observations.chain: provoked year by year → wept, would not eat (1Sa 1:7) · poured out her soul, "Go in peace" → ate, face no longer sad (1:15–18)
observations.parties: Peninnah; Hannah; Elkanah; Eli; the Lord
observations.meaning: one root names the rival's act (kāʿas, "provoke … grievously") and what Hannah carries (kaʿas, "vexation"). It shows in weeping and not eating, and it ends when she has poured out her soul and Eli speaks peace.
observations.implication: already in 10.1 and 11 (D). What unit 3 adds: the same root is the one used 44 times for people provoking God (§A.6).
observations.note: October disposition: D; W (the God side of the root); also appears: 10.1, 11 (D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: What one person is to another: heavier than sand.
observations.chain: vexation weighed → heavier than the sand of the sea → "therefore my words have been rash" (Job 6:2–3)
observations.parties: the fool; Job; a son, his father and mother; a husband and wife
observations.meaning: kaʿas is weighed: heavier than sand in the proverb (a fool's provocation) and in Job (his own vexation). A son can be it to his parents; a wife can be it to her husband.
observations.implication: the same picture, weight beyond sand, is used for the provocation that comes from another and the vexation borne. I set them side by side (R). Job 6:4 (the next verse) is AG-85.

observations.text: Vexation borne within: eye, soul, body, heart, night.
observations.chain: foes → eye wastes away (Psa 6:7) · toil → vexation → heart does not rest at night (Ecc 2:22–23)
observations.parties: David; Job; the Preacher; the toiler
observations.meaning: the noun names what is carried, and the verses place it: the eye, the soul and body, the members, the heart, the nights. Causes are named: foes, distress, toil. Ecc 11:10 says it can be removed from the heart.
observations.implication: already in 10.1 for Psa 6:7, Job 17:7 and Ecc 2:23 (D). Psa 31:9 and Ecc 11:10 add soul with body, and the command to remove it. Psa 31:10 ("my life is spent with sorrow") and Ecc 5:16–17 are death-side.
observations.note: October disposition: D; W (Psa 31:9; Ecc 11:10); Psa 31:10, Ecc 5:16–17 H (OT-08); also appears: 10.1 (D); 07 (Job 17:7: D); 05 (soul) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Vexation that God sees; vexation that comes with wisdom; sorrow that makes the heart glad.
observations.chain: God sees vexation → takes it into his hands → the helpless commits himself (Psa 10:14) · much wisdom → much vexation (Ecc 1:18) · sadness of face → heart made glad (Ecc 7:3)
observations.parties: God; the helpless, the fatherless; the Preacher
observations.meaning: God is said to see vexation and to take it into his hands (Psa 10:14). The Preacher sets vexation beside wisdom (Ecc 1:18), and calls kaʿas ("Sorrow") better than laughter (Ecc 7:3), in the setting of "the house of mourning" (7:2).
observations.implication: in Ecc 7:3 the word for vexation is something that works good in the heart (10.1 and 11 already state this, D). Psa 10:14 is new: vexation seen and taken in hand by God. OT-06 (God's hand). Ecc 7:2 "this is the end of all mankind" is death-side.
observations.note: October disposition: D; W (Psa 10:14, Ecc 1:18); Ecc 7:2 H (OT-08); also appears: 10.1, 11 (Ecc 7:3: D); 10.2 (knowing); OT-06 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The fool's vexation: shown at once, lodged, and killing.
observations.chain: quick in spirit → anger lodges in the heart of fools (Ecc 7:9) · vexation → kills the fool (Job 5:2)
observations.parties: the fool, the prudent; Eliphaz
observations.setting: Ecc 7:8, "the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit". Job 5:2 is spoken by Eliphaz (Job 4:1).
observations.meaning: in the fool it is quick and shown at once, lodged in the heart, and fatal. The prudent "ignores an insult".
observations.implication: already in 10.1, 06, 08 and 11 (D). The speaker of Job 5:2 is Eliphaz, whose words about God the Lord later says were not right (Job 42:7). That verdict is about speech concerning God; I do not apply it to this proverb, and record the speaker only. Job 5:2 is death-side.
observations.note: October disposition: D; Job 5:2 H (OT-08); also appears: 06, 08, 10.1, 11, 12 (D) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit3-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Two hits with no anger.
observations.meaning: Neh 3:20: the hit sits on "repaired", and the ESV verse has no anger word. Psa 58:9: ḥārôn is the burning of thorns.
observations.implication: the heat is in the word again (2W). Data.

observations.text: Wrath that goes out and comes upon.
observations.chain: help the wicked → wrath has gone out (2Ch 19:2) · abandoned the house, served the Asherim → wrath came (24:18) · wrath came → an object of horror (29:8)
observations.parties: God; Jehoshaphat; Jehu the seer; Judah's officials; Hezekiah
observations.setting: Chronicles, a seer to King Jehoshaphat (2Ch 19:2); the narrator after Joash's officials served the Asherim (24:18); Hezekiah to the Levites (29:8).
observations.meaning: the noun qeṣep̄ is spoken of as going out from the Lord and arriving on people. Each time the speaker names what brought it.
observations.implication: the narrative speaks of the wrath as moving between God and the people, with the cause and the arrival in one sentence.

observations.text: The hard heart named as the cause.
observations.chain: hearts diamond-hard, lest they hear → therefore great anger (Zec 7:12) · they would not hear → I would not hear (7:13) · blesses himself in his heart → anger will smoke against that man (Deu 29:19–20)
observations.parties: God; the fathers; the prophets; the Spirit; "that man"
observations.setting: Zechariah's account of the fathers (Zec 7:11–13); the covenant warning to one man in Moab (Deu 29:19–20).
observations.meaning: both verses put the heart first and the anger after it. In Deuteronomy the verb is "smoke" (ʿāšan).
observations.implication: the anger is stated as the answer to a heart that shut itself (extends AG-11 and Ch 13). Zec 7:13 adds that God answers the closed ear in kind.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Zec 7:12); W (Deu 29:20); also appears: 4; 10.2; 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Heard, then full of wrath.
observations.chain: spoke against God → the Lord heard → full of wrath, a fire kindled (Psa 78:19–21) · because they did not believe (78:22) · heard your words → angered → swore (Deu 1:34–35)
observations.parties: God; Jacob, Israel; the spies' generation
observations.setting: Psalm 78's retelling of the wilderness ("Can God spread a table in the wilderness?", 78:19); Moses's retelling after the spies (Deu 1:34).
observations.meaning: ʿābar, "full of wrath", is the verb of passing over or overflowing; here it follows God hearing the people's words. The reason is stated: unbelief and distrust.
observations.implication: the provocation in these verses is speech, heard.

observations.text: God against his own city.
observations.chain: fight against you → strike down man and beast (Jer 21:5–6)
observations.parties: God; Zedekiah; Jerusalem
observations.setting: Jeremiah's answer to Zedekiah's request (Jer 21:4–6); the covenant curse (Deu 29:28).
observations.meaning: the three words stand together (ʾaph, ḥēmāh, qeṣep̄). The arm and hand that brought them out are turned against them.
observations.implication: already in Ch 13 and 11 (Jer 21:5). Touches OT-06.
observations.note: October disposition: D; also appears: 11; 13; OT-06 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: No one stood in the breach.
observations.chain: sought a man … found none → therefore poured out my indignation (Eze 22:30–31) · move the landmark → pour out my wrath like water (Hos 5:10)
observations.parties: God; the princes, priests, prophets; the one not found
observations.setting: Ezekiel 22, after its list of prophets, priests, princes and people of the land (22:25–29); Hosea on the princes who "move the landmark" (Hos 5:10).
observations.meaning: Eze 22:30–31 states the wrath as following the absence of anyone to stand between.
observations.implication: extends 4E (those who do stand: AG-159, AG-160). Read with them in the overview, not joined here.

observations.text: Under the wrath, no one spares another.
observations.chain: wrath → land scorched → no one spares another (Isa 9:19) → devour, not satisfied (9:20)
observations.parties: God; the people
observations.setting: the refrain poem (Isa 9:8–10:4), "For all this his anger has not turned away" (Isa 9:12; 10:4; unit 1 AG-30).
observations.meaning: the verse states the wrath and, in the same breath, people turning on each other with a hunger that is not satisfied.
observations.implication: the wrath is stated as the setting of the people's own consuming of each other; the verse does not say God does it.

observations.text: A king in anger.
observations.chain: as AN-81
observations.parties: God; Israel; the king
observations.meaning: Unit 1 / AN-81: what the people asked for, answered in anger.

observations.text: Provoked to wrath: remember it.
observations.chain: provoked to wrath → ready to destroy you (Deu 9:8) · fathers angered God → given into Nebuchadnezzar's hand → house destroyed (Ezr 5:12) · purposed disaster, did not relent → so again purposed good → fear not (Zec 8:14–15)
observations.parties: God; the fathers; Moses; the exiles; Tattenai's men; Zechariah
observations.setting: Moses to the new generation (Deu 9:7–8, 22), in the speech that warns "Do not say in your heart … 'because of my righteousness'" (Deu 9:4; AN-90); the returned exiles to a Persian governor (Ezr 5:12); Zechariah (Zec 8:14–15).
observations.meaning: the provocation is kept as a memory to be spoken: to the children, to outsiders, and as the ground of a new promise.
observations.implication: extends AG-11 and AG-103 (the measure added to). Zec 8:14–15 sets the old purpose and the new purpose side by side, and ends with "fear not".
observations.note: October disposition: W (Deu 9:7 D in 10.3); also appears: 10.3 (remembering); 10.12 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: A guard set so that wrath does not come.
observations.chain: Levites camp around → no wrath on the congregation (Num 1:53) · keep guard → never again wrath (18:5)
observations.parties: God; the Levites; the congregation; the outsider
observations.setting: the ordering of the camp (Num 1:51–53: "if any outsider comes near, he shall be put to death"); after Korah (Num 18:5).
observations.meaning: people are posted around the holy place for the sake of the whole people.
observations.implication: the wrath is spoken of as kept away by an ordered nearness to the holy (AN-79). Life-and-death side (1:51) held, OT-08.

observations.text: An oath, a warning, a decree, a vow.
observations.chain: sworn oath → let them live, lest wrath (Jos 9:20) · warn them → not incur guilt, wrath not come on you and your brothers (2Ch 19:10) · mouth leads into sin → God angry at your voice → destroy the work of your hands (Ecc 5:6) → God is the one you must fear (5:7)
observations.parties: God; the leaders, the congregation; the Gibeonites; the judges and their brothers; Artaxerxes; the one who vows
observations.setting: the leaders keep a sworn word to the Gibeonites though deceived, and "all the congregation murmured" (Jos 9:18–20); Jehoshaphat's charge to his judges, "in the fear of the Lord, in faithfulness, and with your whole heart" (2Ch 19:9–10); Artaxerxes' decree (Ezr 7:23); the Preacher on vows (Ecc 5:4–7).
observations.meaning: four speakers, of whom one is a Persian king, act or speak with God's wrath in view. The Preacher's case is the mouth: "Let not your mouth lead you into sin".
observations.implication: the wrath is reckoned with in advance, by an Israelite leader, a judge, a foreign king and a man making a vow.
observations.note: October disposition: W (Jos 9:20 D); also appears: 10.5; 10.10 (Jos 9:20) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Mourning held back lest wrath come.
observations.chain: as AN-80
observations.parties: Moses; Aaron and his sons; the congregation
observations.meaning: Unit 3 / AN-79, AN-80: grief withheld near the holy. Life-and-death side held (OT-08).

observations.text: One acts, and all bear it.
observations.chain: proud heart → wrath came on him and Judah (2Ch 32:25) · humbled himself → wrath did not come in his days (32:26) · rebel today → tomorrow angry with the whole congregation (Jos 22:18)
observations.parties: God; Moses and Aaron; Korah; Achan; Joab, David; Hezekiah, Jerusalem
observations.setting: Moses and Aaron on their faces after "that I may consume them in a moment" (Num 16:21–22); Phinehas and the chiefs to the eastern tribes (Jos 22:18–20); the Chronicler (1Ch 27:24; 2Ch 32:24–26).
observations.meaning: the verses state wrath reaching many through one: one man's sin, one man's theft, one man's count, one king's proud heart. Moses and Aaron appeal to God by a title that names him over every spirit. In Hezekiah's case the heart turns both ways, and the wrath follows each.
observations.implication: extends AN-78. New: the title in the appeal (Num 16:22), and Hezekiah's two movements of heart in two verses.
observations.note: October disposition: D (2Ch 32:25–26; Num 16:22); W (Jos 22, 1Ch 27:24); also appears: 7 (Num 16:22); 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Heard for the people; not heard for himself.
observations.chain: afraid of the anger → the Lord listened (Deu 9:19) · angry with me because of you → would not listen → "Enough from you" → go up to Pisgah and look (3:26–27)
observations.parties: Moses; God; the people; Joshua (3:28)
observations.setting: Moses's two retellings in Deuteronomy: the calf (9:18–19) and his own plea to cross the Jordan ("Please let me go over and see the good land", 3:25).
observations.meaning: the same man pleads both times. For the people he is afraid and is heard. For himself the Lord is angry "because of you" and says "Enough".
observations.implication: Moses names his own fear of God's anger (fear strand, 10.12). The anger at Moses is tied by Moses to the people ("because of you"); the verse does not explain it further (AG-181 has Meribah).
observations.note: October disposition: D (9:19); W (3:26); also appears: 10.12; 13 (9:19) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Atonement carried into the midst.
observations.chain: wrath gone out → plague begun → atonement → stood between → plague stopped (Num 16:46–48)
observations.parties: Moses; Aaron; the congregation; the dead and the living
observations.setting: after the earth swallowed Korah's company and the congregation grumbled (Num 16:41–45).
observations.meaning: Moses reads the wrath as already gone out, and sends Aaron at a run. Aaron stands, and the plague stops.
observations.implication: with AG-151 (no one found to stand in the breach), the verses show what standing between means. "Between the dead and the living" is held for OT-08.
observations.note: October disposition: W; H (the life-death phrase); also appears: 10.9; OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: An angel asks "how long".
observations.chain: how long … angry these seventy years? → answered gracious and comforting words (Zec 1:12–13) → returned with mercy (1:16)
observations.parties: the angel of the Lord; the riders; God; Jerusalem; Zechariah
observations.setting: Zechariah's first vision (Zec 1:8–17): the riders report "all the earth remains at rest".
observations.meaning: the one who asks is the angel of the Lord, and the anger is measured in years. The answer is jealousy for Jerusalem and anger at the nations "at ease" (AG-167).
observations.implication: ruling 6.2: an angel stands among the parties to God's anger, as an asker.

observations.text: For a moment, and forever.
observations.chain: anger for a moment → hid my face; everlasting love → compassion (Isa 54:8) · struck in wrath → mercy in favour (60:10)
observations.parties: God; Zion as a deserted wife; foreigners who build
observations.setting: Isaiah 54 ("like a wife deserted and grieved in spirit", 54:6); Isaiah 60.
observations.meaning: the anger has a length (a moment) and the compassion a length (everlasting), stated side by side; the oath is likened to Noah's (54:9).
observations.implication: extends AG-46. Isa 54:8 is in Ch 13 and 10.9. Duration is one of the governing circumstances (§L.3).
observations.note: October disposition: D (54:8); W (54:9; 60:10); also appears: 13; 10.9 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The reason given is the human spirit.
observations.chain: not always angry, for the spirit would grow faint (Isa 57:16) · angry, struck → went on backsliding → I will heal him (57:17–18)
observations.parties: God; the contrite and lowly; the backslider; his mourners
observations.meaning: AN-82. Already in Ch 2, 13, 14 and 10.9. The breath of life side is held (OT-08).

observations.text: Gathered back from the wrath.
observations.chain: drove them in my anger → gather, bring back, dwell in safety (Jer 32:37) → my people (32:38)
observations.parties: God; the exiles
observations.setting: Jeremiah in the siege (32:36), the day he bought the field.
observations.meaning: the three words for anger name the driving out, and the same sentence turns to bringing back.
observations.implication: extends AG-162: the place of the anger is named within the promise.

observations.text: The indignation has an end.
observations.chain: fury will come to an end → be not afraid (Isa 10:24–25) · enter your chambers … until the fury has passed by (26:20)
observations.parties: God; "my people"; Daniel and the one who speaks to him; the king who exalts himself
observations.setting: Daniel's visions (8:19; 11:36); Isaiah's song (26:20–21) and his word to Zion (10:24–25).
observations.meaning: zaʿam, God's indignation, is spoken of as a period with an end that is decreed. In Isaiah the end is the reason given for not being afraid, and for hiding "for a little while".
observations.implication: time governs God's anger in these verses as it governs the human anger in AG-187. The people are told how to wait inside it.
observations.note: October disposition: D (26:20); W; also appears: 10.11 (Isa 26:20); 10.12; 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The rod whose heart has its own aim.
observations.chain: sent against a godless nation (Isa 10:6) · but it is in his heart to destroy (10:7)
observations.parties: God; Assyria; Babylon's attackers; "a godless nation"
observations.setting: Isaiah 10 and 13; Jeremiah 50.
observations.meaning: a nation is called the rod and the weapon of God's anger, and in the same passage its own heart is said to intend something else.
observations.implication: the instrument has an inner being of its own, and Isaiah speaks to it (Isa 10:12, "the boastful look in his eyes").

observations.text: The instrument goes beyond.
observations.chain: gave them into your hand → you showed no mercy (Isa 47:6) → did not lay to heart (47:7) · angry but a little → they furthered the disaster → exceedingly angry with them (Zec 1:15) · gave them into your hand → killed in a rage → "Have you not sins of your own?" (2Ch 28:9–10)
observations.parties: God; Babylon; the nations at ease; Israel's army; Oded; the captives
observations.setting: to Babylon (Isa 47:5–7); in Zechariah's vision (1:15); Oded to Israel's army (2Ch 28:9–10).
observations.meaning: in each, God's anger gave a people into another's hand, and the one given power is then charged for what it added: no mercy, furthering the disaster, a rage of its own.
observations.implication: each of the three verses states it. The rage in 2Ch 28:9 is zaʿap̄, the instrument's own; Oded's question turns them to their own sins.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Zec 1:15; 2Ch 28:9); W (Isa 47:6); also appears: 11; 10.1; 10.9 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Wrath in the lips, tongue and voice.
observations.chain: voice heard → Assyrians terror-stricken (Isa 30:30–31) · his wrath → earth quakes, nations cannot endure (Jer 10:10)
observations.parties: God; Assyria; the nations; the earth, rocks
observations.setting: Isaiah 30 against Assyria; Jeremiah 10 against the idols ("he is the living God", 10:10); Nahum 1 on Nineveh.
observations.meaning: God's fury is placed in his lips and tongue, heard in his voice, and seen in his arm. The verses state what it does to those before it: terror, quaking, no one able to stand.
observations.implication: the wrath reaches the nations by voice as well as by blow. The terror it causes is the fear strand's one who makes afraid (10.12).
observations.note: October disposition: D (Jer 10:10; Nah 1:6); W (Isa 30); also appears: 10.5; 10.12; 2 (Jer 10:10); 13 (Nah 1:6) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Indignation every day, and the heart that rejoices.
observations.chain: does not repent → God will whet his sword (Psa 7:12) · indignation against enemies → your heart shall rejoice (Isa 66:14) · angry forever (with Edom) → your eyes shall see → "Great is the Lord" (Mal 1:4–5)
observations.parties: God; the wicked; his servants; Edom; Israel
observations.setting: David's plea (Psa 7:9–12); the last chapter of Isaiah (66:14); Malachi's opening, "I have loved you" (Mal 1:2–5).
observations.meaning: the indignation is a judge's, daily, and turns on whether a man repents. The same act that is indignation to enemies is a heart's joy and flourishing bones to his servants, and makes Israel say "Great is the Lord".
observations.implication: ruling 6.2: those for whom the anger acts are named with their inner response.
observations.note: October disposition: W; also appears: 10.9; OT-06 (Isa 66:14) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Creation and the nations before it.
observations.chain: marched in fury → went out for the salvation of your people (Hab 3:12–13)
observations.parties: God; the nations; rivers, sea, earth; destroying angels; Gog
observations.meaning: Units 1 and 3 (3C). Habakkuk adds "You went out for the salvation of your people" (3:13). Psa 78:49 names angels as the bearers of the wrath to Egypt (ruling 6.2: spirits among the parties).

observations.text: Riches do not deliver in the day of wrath.
observations.chain: day of wrath → riches do not profit; righteousness delivers (Pro 11:4) · silver cannot deliver → cannot satisfy hunger → it was the stumbling block (Eze 7:19)
observations.parties: God; the rich; the righteous
observations.setting: a proverb (Pro 11:4); Ezekiel 7, "the end has come" (Eze 7:6); Zephaniah 1.
observations.meaning: three verses, each stating it in its own words: what was trusted gives nothing on that day. Ezekiel adds that the silver itself had been "the stumbling block of their iniquity".
observations.implication: the day of wrath shows what a person trusted. "Delivers from death" is held for OT-08.
observations.note: October disposition: W; H (death side); also appears: 10.6 (wanting); OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The day named, and on whom it falls.
observations.chain: expectation of the wicked → ends in wrath (Pro 11:23) · the Lord angry with him → falls into the pit (Pro 22:14)
observations.parties: God; the evil man; Job and his friends; the righteous; the forbidden woman
observations.setting: Zephaniah 1; Job answering his friends (21:29–30): he says travellers report the evil man spared; the speaker is Job, against his friends' account; the Proverbs.
observations.meaning: Zephaniah names the day by what is felt in it (distress, anguish, gloom). Job disputes what the friends say happens on it. The proverbs set the end of a desire or expectation in good or in wrath, and name the one God is angry with as the one who falls into the pit.
observations.implication: Job 21:30 is Job's complaint, not a statement of the book's teaching.

observations.text: Called down.
observations.parties: the psalmist; enemies
observations.meaning: Unit 3 (3H).

observations.text: In flesh and bones, with his sin beside it.
observations.chain: your indignation → no soundness in my flesh; my sin → no health in my bones (Psa 38:3) · your indignation → ashes like bread, tears in drink (Psa 102:9–10)
observations.parties: David; the afflicted; God
observations.setting: David's psalm "for the memorial offering" (Psa 38); the prayer of one afflicted, when he is faint (Psa 102, title).
observations.meaning: the psalmists name God's indignation as the reason for what is in their flesh, bones, food and drink. Psa 38:3 gives two reasons in one verse: your indignation, my sin.
observations.implication: the body is where these psalms feel God's anger (extends AG-23, AG-87).
observations.note: October disposition: D (38:3); W; also appears: 7 (Psa 38:3) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Days under it.
observations.chain: days pass under your wrath → years end like a sigh (Psa 90:9)
observations.parties: Moses; God
observations.meaning: Psalm 90, of Moses (title). In Ch 2 and 13. The life-and-death side is held (OT-08).
observations.note: October disposition: D; H (OT-08); also appears: 2; 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The smoke word.
observations.parties: Asaph; God; the people; the mountains
observations.setting: Asaph's laments (Psa 74; 80); Sinai (Exo 19:18); praise of the Creator (Psa 104:32; 144:5).
observations.meaning: ʿāšan is the word for Sinai smoking when God came down, and for mountains smoking at his touch. In Psa 74:1 and Deu 29:20 it is the word for his anger toward his people. In Psa 80:4 the ESV renders it "be angry", and it is against "your people's prayers".
observations.implication: the same verb is God's coming down and his anger. Psa 80:4 asks why prayer itself meets it; the psalm answers with a refrain, "Restore us … let your face shine" (80:3).
observations.note: October disposition: D; W (the smoke word); also appears: 13 (Psa 74:1; 80:4); 15 (Exo 19:18) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Borne until he pleads my cause.
observations.chain: sinned → bear the indignation → until he pleads my cause → bring me out to the light (Mic 7:9)
observations.parties: Micah's speaker, the enemy; the man of Lamentations; Ethan (Psa 89); the anointed
observations.setting: Micah's closing ("Rejoice not over me, O my enemy; when I fall, I shall rise", 7:8); Lamentations 3 and its last verse (5:22); Psalm 89, after the promise "His offspring shall endure forever" (89:36).
observations.meaning: Micah's speaker bears it with a stated reason (I have sinned) and a stated end (until he pleads my cause). Lamentations ends on the question. Psalm 89 sets God's anger against his own promise, and does not resolve it in the verse.
observations.implication: three different ways of bearing it, each in its own setting.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Mic 7:9; Lam 3:1; 5:22); W (Psa 89:38); also appears: 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The clay pleads.
observations.parties: the remnant; God
observations.meaning: AN-88. The plea follows "we are the clay, and you are our potter" (Isa 64:8). Isa 64:5 states the anger first and the sinning after; I record the order as it stands, not a cause.

observations.text: Denouncing only where God has.
observations.parties: Balak; Balaam; God; the peoples; the judge who acquits
observations.setting: Balaam's first oracle (Num 23:7–8); a proverb (24:24–25); Micah on false weights (6:10).
observations.meaning: zāʿam is also the spoken curse, "denounce". Balaam cannot go beyond God's own verdict. In the proverb the peoples' denouncing falls on the one who calls the wicked right.
observations.implication: AN §L.2. Num 23:8 is in 11 and 10.5.

observations.text: Filled with his indignation.
observations.chain: your hand upon me → filled with indignation → sat alone (Jer 15:17)
observations.parties: Jeremiah; God
observations.meaning: Already in 10.9 (those who carry God's anger inside them). The hand touches OT-06.
observations.note: October disposition: D; also appears: 10.9; OT-06 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Meribah: the quarrel kept in a name, and what it did to Moses.
observations.chain: angered him at Meribah → it went ill with Moses → made his spirit bitter → spoke rashly (Psa 106:32–33) · rebelled at Meribah → Aaron shall not enter the land (Num 20:24)
observations.parties: the people; God; Moses; Aaron; Levi
observations.setting: the two quarrels (Exo 17; Num 20); God's word to Moses and Aaron (Num 20:24; 27:14; Deu 32:51, "because you did not treat me as holy"); the Psalms' retellings (Psa 95:8; 81:7; 106:32–33); Levi's blessing (Deu 33:8).
observations.meaning: the place name holds the quarrel. Psalm 106 states what passed from the people to Moses: they angered God, they embittered Moses's spirit, and he spoke rashly. God's word names Moses's and Aaron's part as rebellion and failing to treat him as holy. Psalm 81 calls it God's test, and Psalm 95 a hardened heart (AN-91).
observations.implication: a strife between people and God reaches the leader's spirit and lips. Exo 17:7 and Psa 95:8 are in Ch 12.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Exo 17:7; Psa 95:8); W (Psa 106:32–33; Num 20:24); also appears: 12; 10.5 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The ruler's anger, and those beneath it.
observations.chain: angry → put them in custody (Gen 40:2–3) · refused to come → enraged → counsel → decree (Est 1:12–19) · angry → commanded all the wise men destroyed → they sought Daniel (Dan 2:12–13) · provokes him → forfeits his life (Pro 20:2)
observations.parties: Pharaoh, the cupbearer, the baker; Ahasuerus, Vashti, Memucan; Nebuchadnezzar, the wise men, three Jews; the servant who deals wisely
observations.setting: Joseph's prison (Gen 40:1–3; 41:9–10); Ahasuerus' feast, "when the heart of the king was merry with wine" (Est 1:10–12), and Memucan's counsel (1:16–18); Nebuchadnezzar's demand that no one could meet (Dan 2:10–13); the Proverbs (Pro 19:12; 20:2; 14:35).
observations.meaning: the anger of one who can command is followed at once by a command: custody, a decree, destruction. Those beneath it name it as a lion's growl and speak of it with fear, and Memucan fears the wrath that contempt would spread.
observations.implication: in these verses the anger's reach is set by the angry one's power. Est 1:12 and Pro 19:12 are in 10.1, 11 and 10.10.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Est 1:12; Pro 19:12); W; also appears: 10.1; 11; 10.10; 10.3 (Gen 41:9) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Anger at what was not done as commanded, and how it ended.
observations.chain: did not listen, left till morning → stank → Moses angry (Exo 16:20) · Moses angry → Aaron's answer → Moses heard → approved (Lev 10:16–20) · struck three times and stopped → man of God angry → only three victories (2Ki 13:18–19)
observations.parties: Moses; the people; Aaron, Eleazar, Ithamar; the officers; Elisha; Joash
observations.setting: the manna (Exo 16:19–20); the day Nadab and Abihu died (Lev 10:16–20); after the war on Midian (Num 31:14–16); Elisha's death-bed and the arrows (2Ki 13:18–19).
observations.meaning: the anger of a leader or a prophet at an order not kept. In Lev 10 it is answered: Aaron gives his reason, and Moses, hearing, approves.
observations.implication: Lev 10:20 is a stated case of anger settled by an answer that is heard (the factor the answer it meets, AN §L.3).

observations.text: Angry at a word that crossed what was expected; vexed and sullen.
observations.chain: thought he would come out → angry → went away (2Ki 5:11) → servants' question → dipped → flesh restored (5:13–14) · angry with the priests → leprosy broke out (2Ch 26:19) · Naboth's word → vexed and sullen → lay down, turned away his face, would eat no food (1Ki 21:4)
observations.parties: Naaman, Elisha, the servants; Uzziah, Azariah and the priests; Ahab, Naboth, Jezebel, the prophet
observations.setting: Naaman at Elisha's door (2Ki 5:10–14); Uzziah in the temple after the priests withstood him (2Ch 26:16–20); Ahab after the prophet's sentence (1Ki 20:42–43) and after Naboth's refusal (21:1–5).
observations.meaning: each is angered by a word: a prophet's plain instruction, the priests' rebuke, a neighbour's refusal, a prophet's sentence. Naaman's servants turn him with a gentle question, and he is healed. Uzziah's anger is met by leprosy with the censer still in his hand. Ahab's is turned inward: bed, face to the wall, no food, and Jezebel asks "Why is your spirit so vexed".
observations.implication: the same occasion (a word that crosses the will) and different outcomes, decided by what meets it. Unit 3 AG-137 (Asa, 2Ch 16:10) is the fourth case.
observations.note: October disposition: D (2Ki 5:11; 2Ch 26:19; 1Ki 21:4); W (2Ki 5:13–14; 1Ki 20:43); also appears: 10.1; 11 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Anger at one suspected, or set against.
observations.chain: afraid → withdraw → turn back → enraged → take action (Dan 11:30) · "It is a lie" → Irijah would not listen → enraged → beat, imprisoned (Jer 37:14–15) · became angry → sought to lay hands on the king (Est 2:21)
observations.parties: the Philistine commanders, Achish, David; Bigthan and Teresh, Mordecai, Esther; Irijah, the officials, Jeremiah; the king of the north
observations.setting: David among the Philistines (1Sa 29:3–5, with the song "David his ten thousands"); the plot Mordecai uncovered (Est 2:21–22); Jeremiah at the gate (Jer 37:13–15); the king of the north (Dan 11:28–30, "his heart shall be set against the holy covenant").
observations.meaning: the anger is at someone suspected or opposed, and in two verses it moves straight to the hands (lay hands on, beat). In Daniel, fear comes first, then withdrawal, then rage.
observations.implication: Dan 11:30 states fear turning into rage (fear strand, 10.12). Jer 37:14–15 sets a denial unheard beside the officials' rage.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Jer 37:15; Dan 11:30); W; also appears: 10.1; 10.12 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Anger turned against God.
observations.chain: hungry → enraged → speak contemptuously against their king and their God (Isa 8:21) · folly → way ruined → heart rages against the Lord (Pro 19:3)
observations.parties: the people; their king; God; the man and his folly
observations.setting: after "should not a people inquire of their God? Should they inquire of the dead on behalf of the living?" (Isa 8:19–22); a proverb (Pro 19:3).
observations.meaning: in Isaiah, hunger and distress lead to rage and contempt spoken against king and God. In the proverb the man's own folly ruins his way, and his heart rages at the Lord, not at the folly.
observations.implication: both verses state the person's anger turned toward God; the proverb states that its target is not its cause. Pro 19:3 is in 10.9 and 12.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Pro 19:3); W (Isa 8:21); also appears: 10.9; 12 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Anger kept forever, cursed.
observations.chain: in their anger killed men → cursed be their anger → I will divide them (Gen 49:6–7) · cast off pity, kept his wrath forever → I will not revoke the punishment (Amo 1:11) · sows injustice → reap calamity; rod of his fury will fail (Pro 22:8)
observations.parties: Jacob; Simeon and Levi; Edom and his brother; Babylon's king; the unjust
observations.setting: Jacob's last words to Simeon and Levi (Gen 49:5–7); the oracle against Edom (Amo 1:11); the taunt over Babylon's king (Isa 14:4–6); a proverb (Pro 22:8).
observations.meaning: Jacob curses the anger, not the sons, and asks that his soul not join their council. Amos charges Edom with anger that "tore perpetually" and wrath he "kept … forever", with pity cast off.
observations.implication: I read the length here as the charge itself: unceasing, perpetual, forever. Set beside God's anger for a moment (AG-162) in the overview, not joined here. Amo 1:11 is in 10.1 and 11; Isa 14:6 in 10.10.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Amo 1:11; Isa 14:6); W (Gen 49:7); also appears: 10.1; 11; 10.10 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The overflow: wrath, and pride.
observations.parties: the scoffer; Moab; Ephraim's princes; God; Job
observations.meaning: AN §L.2. Already in 11 §4 "Overflow". ʿebrāh is "pride" in Pro 21:24 and "insolence" in Isa 16:6 and Jer 48:30; zaʿam is "insolence" in Hos 7:16. God's challenge to Job uses ʿebrāh for the anger that brings the proud down.

observations.text: The enemies' fury.
observations.chain: their anger kindled → swallowed us alive → the raging waters (Psa 124:3–5)
observations.parties: David; enemies; God; the poor
observations.setting: David (Psa 7:6); "If it had not been the Lord who was on our side" (Psa 124:1–5); Habakkuk's prayer (Hab 3:14).
observations.meaning: the enemies' ʿebrāh is met by God's ʾaph: the psalmist asks one anger to rise against another. Psalm 124 pictures the enemies' kindled anger (unit 3) as raging waters; Habakkuk pictures warriors as a whirlwind.
observations.implication: extends unit 3 face 3S.
observations.note: October disposition: D (7:6); W; also appears: 2 (Psa 7:6) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Borne within, all his days.
observations.parties: the one who toils
observations.meaning: The Preacher on the man who toils for the wind (Ecc 5:16–17). qeṣep̄ here is a man's, beside kaʿas (unit 3 AG-143). Life-and-death side (5:16) held, OT-08.

observations.text: Strife: where it comes from, what holds it, what ends it.
observations.chain: perverted heart → sowing discord (Pro 6:14) · quarrelsome man → kindling strife (26:21) · no whisperer → quarreling ceases (26:20) · tarry over wine → strife, wounds (23:29–30) · backbiting tongue → angry looks (25:23) · no strife, for we are kinsmen → choose the land (Gen 13:8–9)
observations.parties: Abram, Lot and the herdsmen; the worthless man; the quarrelsome man; brothers; the drinker; the backbiter
observations.setting: Abram and Lot's herdsmen (Gen 13:7–9); the Proverbs.
observations.meaning: the verses name a source for strife (a perverted heart, a quarrelsome man, wine, a backbiting tongue), what it is like once in place (bars of a castle, an offended brother), and what ends it (the lot; Abram giving Lot the choice of the land; "where there is no whisperer, quarreling ceases", Pro 26:20).
observations.implication: strife is spoken of as kindled, like fire (Pro 26:20–21), in the heat picture of unit 2. Gen 13:8, Pro 18:19 are in 10.10.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Gen 13:8; Pro 18:19); W; also appears: 10.10; 10.5 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The quarrelsome wife.
observations.parties: a wife; her husband
observations.setting: five proverbs.
observations.meaning: the quarrel is pictured as a dripping that does not stop, and the way out named is distance (the housetop corner, the desert).
observations.implication: in these sayings the quarrel's mark is that it continues. Pro 21:19 is also unit 3 (3X, "fretful").
observations.note: October disposition: D (21:9; 27:15); W; also appears: 10.10 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Hostility forbidden, and taken up.
observations.chain: I have given Ar to Lot's sons → do not harass (Deu 2:9) · obey his voice → I will be an adversary to your adversaries (Exo 23:22)
observations.parties: God; Israel; Moab, Ammon; the angel; the Jews of Persia
observations.setting: the march past Moab and Ammon (Deu 2:9, 19); the angel sent ahead (Exo 23:20–22).
observations.meaning: ṣûr is hostility. Israel is forbidden it toward Lot's sons, for a stated reason: God gave them their land. God takes it up for Israel, on a stated condition.
observations.implication: not an anger word in these verses; hostility, with its limit and its permission stated. Est 8:11 is the same word in a decree.

observations.text: The face that falls.
observations.chain: not look on you in anger, for I am merciful → only acknowledge your guilt (Jer 3:12–13)
observations.parties: Cain; God; faithless Israel
observations.setting: Cain (Gen 4:5–6; unit 3 AG-131, AG-138); Jeremiah's call to the north (Jer 3:11–13).
observations.meaning: the tags show the same pair, "fall" and "face", in both verses. In Gen 4:5 Cain's face falls. In Jer 3:12 the ESV's "look on you in anger" renders God's I will not cause my face to fall on you.
observations.implication: the phrase for Cain's anger is the phrase God uses when he withholds his. The reason given is "for I am merciful".
observations.note: October disposition: D (Gen 4:5); NS (the pair, for 10.13); also appears: 10.1; 7; 15 (Gen 4:5) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The same words, with no anger: troubled faces.
observations.chain: they were troubled → "Why are your faces downcast?" → "We have had dreams" (Gen 40:6–8) · mind greatly troubled → "who of us is for the king of Israel?" (2Ki 6:11)
observations.parties: the cupbearer and baker, Joseph; the chief eunuch, Daniel; Darius; the king of Syria, Elisha; Zion
observations.setting: the two dreamers (Gen 40:5–8); the chief eunuch's fear of the king (Dan 1:10); Darius trapped by his own decree (Dan 6:14); the king of Syria whose plans Elisha keeps telling (2Ki 6:8–12); Zion (Isa 54:11).
observations.meaning: zāʿap̄, which is rage in 2Ch 26:19, is here a downcast face (Gen 40:6) and a thinner face (Dan 1:10). sāʿar, the storm, is a king's troubled mind and a city's affliction. None of these verses is about anger.
observations.implication: a change of character within one root (#1919). Correction: Ch 11 §4 Storm calls 2Ki 6:11 the angry king's mind. The verse says "greatly troubled"; no anger word is in it.
observations.note: October disposition: RS (Ch 11 "Storm" bullet); also appears: 11 §4 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Lament (qînāh).
observations.chain: the Lord has rejected the generation of his wrath → raise a lamentation (Jer 7:29)
observations.parties: David; Jeremiah; the singing men and women; the women and daughters; Ezekiel; Amos
observations.setting: laments for kings and friends (2Sa 1:17; 2Ch 35:25); laments commanded by God over Judah, Tyre, Egypt and the princes (Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Amos); the scroll "written … words of lamentation and mourning and woe" (Eze 2:10).
observations.meaning: qînāh is a lament, a set song of grief, made, taught and written down. It is not an anger word. In one verse (Jer 7:29) it is raised because of God's wrath.
observations.implication: the lament is grief's form, not anger's. AN-80 already has Jer 7:29. The association with grief is for cross-cluster analysis (§F.11).
observations.note: October disposition: W (Jer 7:29 D); data note; also appears: 10.1 (mourning); M03 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit4-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: No anger in the verse.
observations.meaning: The sea's zaʿap̄ (Jon 1:15); the storm (sāʿar) of the sea and the scattering (Jon 1:11, 13; Zec 7:14; Hos 13:3); two words from a different root (Hos 10:7; Joe 1:7); Meribah-kadesh as a border (Eze 47:19; 48:28); smoking mountains (AG-176). Data, not narrative. Zec 7:14 follows "great anger came" (7:12) and states what God did; the storm word is not the anger.

observations.text: Great wrath, source not named.
observations.chain: offered his son on the wall → great wrath against Israel → they withdrew (2Ki 3:27)
observations.parties: the king of Moab, his son; Israel
observations.meaning: AN-H4. The verse does not say whose wrath. Recorded, not interpreted.

observations.text: Revealed from heaven against those who suppress the truth.
observations.chain: suppress the truth → wrath revealed against them (1:18) · what can be known is plain, God has shown it (1:19)
observations.parties: God; "men" who suppress the truth
observations.setting: the opening of Paul's argument in Romans, after "the righteousness of God is revealed" (Rom 1:17).
observations.meaning: the wrath is revealed, in the present tense, and its object is named by what people do with the truth: they hold it down. In the same passage God gives them up to the lusts of their own hearts (1:24).
observations.implication: I read the giving up (1:24) as the setting in which the wrath is described; Paul states the "therefore" from what precedes it (1:21–23), not from 1:18, and I do not join the two.

observations.text: Stored up by a hard and impenitent heart.
observations.chain: hard and impenitent heart → storing up wrath (2:5) · self-seeking, not obey the truth → wrath and fury (2:8)
observations.parties: God; the one who judges; the self-seeking
observations.meaning: the heart that does not repent is said to store up wrath for yourself: the person is the one adding to it. Kindness is named first, and its purpose. Rom 2:8 sets orgē and thymos together, as the Hebrew set ʾaph and ḥēmāh (unit 1).
observations.implication: extends AG-11 (the measure added to).
observations.note: October disposition: D (2:5); W (2:4, 8); also appears: 12; 13 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Remains on him.
observations.chain: does not obey the Son → shall not see life → the wrath of God remains on him (3:36)
observations.parties: God; the Son; the one who believes; the one who does not obey
observations.setting: the close of John 3, after "The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand" (3:35).
observations.meaning: the wrath is spoken of as already resting on a person, and staying. Its contrast is life.
observations.implication: the life-and-death side is held (OT-08).
observations.note: October disposition: W; H (life side); also appears: OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Coming, because of these things; and the same words told to be put away.
observations.chain: because of these things → the wrath of God comes (Eph 5:6) · on account of these → the wrath of God is coming (Col 3:6)
observations.parties: God; the sons of disobedience; the readers
observations.setting: Ephesians 5 and Colossians 3. The these are named in Col 3:5: "sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry".
observations.meaning: the wrath is said to come on account of what people do, and the readers are told they once walked in it. Two verses later, in Colossians, orgē (God's wrath in 3:6) is the first word in the list of what the readers must put away (3:8), and thymos the second.
observations.implication: the same noun names God's wrath and the anger a person is told to put off, in one paragraph. Paul does not explain the link.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Col 3:6, 8); W (Eph 5:6); also appears: 12; 13; 14 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The law brings wrath.
observations.chain: law → wrath; no law → no transgression (4:15)
observations.parties: God; the law; Abraham's offspring
observations.setting: Paul on the promise to Abraham, which came not through the law (Rom 4:13–16).
observations.meaning: the wrath is tied to transgression, and transgression to a law that is known.
observations.implication: a stated condition for the wrath: something given and broken.

observations.text: Come upon them at last.
observations.chain: killed, drove out, hindered → fill up the measure of their sins → wrath has come (1Th 2:15–16)
observations.parties: Paul; those who persecuted; the Gentiles; the churches in Judea
observations.setting: Paul to the Thessalonians, on those in Judea who persecuted the churches there (1Th 2:14).
observations.meaning: a list of deeds, ending in hindering the gospel, so as always to fill up the measure of their sins, and the wrath named as arrived.
observations.implication: the measure filled (AG-11, unit 3 AG-103) appears again in the Greek.

observations.text: Wrath against this people.
observations.parties: Jesus; "this people"; the women
observations.setting: Jesus's words on the fall of Jerusalem (Luk 21:20–24), with "Alas for women who are pregnant".
observations.meaning: distress on the earth and wrath against a people, said together.
observations.implication: read with 5F (the day), not joined.

observations.text: The wilderness retold to a church: the heart, today.
observations.chain: go astray in their heart → provoked (3:10) → swore in my wrath → shall not enter (3:11) · exhort one another every day → none hardened (3:13) · unable to enter because of unbelief (3:19)
observations.parties: the Holy Spirit; God; the fathers; the brothers; "that generation"
observations.setting: Hebrews 3–4 quotes Psalm 95 and says it is the Holy Spirit who speaks it (3:7).
observations.meaning: the provocation is named as a heart that goes astray and does not know his ways; the wrath is an oath (they shall not enter). Hebrews then turns the psalm to its readers: the heart is named three more times (3:12, 13, 15), and the remedy given is people exhorting one another daily.
observations.implication: extends AG-181 (Meribah; Psa 95:8). Ruling 6.2: the brothers are a party to whether a heart hardens. Heb 3:17 ("whose bodies fell in the wilderness") is held for OT-08.
observations.note: October disposition: W; H (3:17); also appears: 12 (hardening); OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Flee from the wrath to come.
observations.chain: who warned you to flee → bear fruit in keeping with repentance (Mat 3:7–8)
observations.parties: John; the Pharisees and Sadducees; the crowds
observations.setting: John the Baptist to the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism (Mat 3:7–8), and to the crowds (Luk 3:7).
observations.meaning: the wrath is ahead; John asks who warned them and tells them what repentance must show.
observations.implication: coming to be baptised is not taken as fruit in itself.

observations.text: Saved from it, delivered, not destined for it.
observations.chain: justified by his blood → saved from the wrath (Rom 5:9) · turned from idols → wait for his Son → delivers us from the wrath (1Th 1:9–10)
observations.parties: God; the Son; "we"; the Thessalonians
observations.meaning: the deliverer is named each time (his blood, his Son, Jesus). In Romans, those delivered were enemies.
observations.implication: Ch 13 holds these; for 10.13 the parties are the deliverer and the delivered, with God the one whose wrath it is.

observations.text: Children of wrath, by nature; but God, rich in mercy.
observations.chain: lived in the passions of our flesh → by nature children of wrath (2:3) · but God, rich in mercy → made us alive (2:4–5)
observations.parties: Paul and the readers; "the rest of mankind"; God
observations.meaning: flesh and mind are named as what was being carried out. Children of wrath is said of "we all", the writer included. The next verse turns on But God.
observations.implication: the life-and-death side ("dead in our trespasses") is held (OT-08).
observations.note: October disposition: D; H (2:5); also appears: 12; 13; 14 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Wrath shown, patience endured.
observations.parties: God; vessels of wrath; vessels of mercy
observations.setting: Paul's answer to "Why does he still find fault?" (Rom 9:19), with the potter and the clay (9:21).
observations.meaning: a question, What if. In one sentence God desires to show his wrath and endures with much patience.
observations.implication: recorded as Paul asks it, not as a statement.

observations.text: Never avenge yourselves; leave it to the wrath of God.
observations.chain: never avenge → leave it to the wrath of God (12:19)
observations.parties: the beloved; the enemy; God
observations.meaning: the person wronged is told to give way to God's wrath and to feed the enemy.

observations.text: The authority carries out God's wrath; conscience beside it.
observations.chain: do wrong → be afraid → he bears the sword (13:4) · be in subjection → to avoid wrath, and for conscience (13:5)
observations.parties: God; the governing authority; the wrongdoer; the one who does good
observations.meaning: a human ruler is named God's servant and the one who carries out his wrath. The reader is given two reasons to be subject: the wrath, and conscience. Fear is named ("be afraid", 13:4).
observations.implication: ruling 6.2: the authority is a party. Rom 12:19 and 13:4 stand a few verses apart; the overview sets them side by side, not joined here. Fear strand: 10.12.

observations.text: Hide us from the wrath of the Lamb.
observations.chain: the great day of their wrath has come → who can stand? (Rev 6:17)
observations.parties: the one on the throne; the Lamb; kings, great ones, generals, rich, powerful, slave and free; mountains and rocks
observations.meaning: the wrath is the Lamb's, and the one on the throne's ("their wrath"). Every rank is named, and all do the same: hide, and ask to be hidden from a face.
observations.implication: the question who can stand is asked in Nah 1:6 (AG-168) as well; a pointer, not a join.

observations.text: The nations raged; your wrath came.
observations.chain: nations raged → but your wrath came → the dead judged, servants rewarded (Rev 11:18)
observations.parties: the nations; kings and rulers; Herod, Pilate; the Lord and his Anointed; David; the Holy Spirit; the elders
observations.setting: the church at prayer after Peter and John are released (Act 4:23–27), quoting Psalm 2 by the Holy Spirit; the elders' worship in Rev 11:16–18.
observations.meaning: the nations' rage is against God and his Anointed. In Acts the church names who gathered (Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles, the peoples of Israel). In Revelation the nations' rage and God's wrath stand in one sentence, joined by but.
observations.implication: ruling 6.2: the nations are an angry party, and their anger is aimed at God. "The time for the dead to be judged" is held (OT-08).
observations.note: October disposition: D (Act 4:25); W (Rev 11:18); H (the dead); also appears: 10.4 (Act 4:25); OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The cup, the winepress, the bowls, and finished.
observations.chain: worships the beast → will drink the wine of God's wrath (14:9–10) · with the last plagues → the wrath of God is finished (15:1) · God remembered Babylon → drain the cup (16:19)
observations.parties: God; the Lamb; angels; one of the four living creatures; the worshipper of the beast; Babylon; the nations; the rider
observations.setting: Revelation 14–19.
observations.meaning: the wrath is pictured as drink (the cup, the wine), harvest (the winepress) and bowls poured out. It is carried by angels and one of the four living creatures. With the last plagues it is finished. "God remembered Babylon" (16:19) is in 10.3.
observations.implication: the drink picture extends unit 2 (ḥēmāh as a drink poured and returned, AN §L.2). The end set for God's anger (AG-165) has its Greek counterpart in finished (15:1).
observations.note: October disposition: D (16:19); W; also appears: 10.3 (16:19) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Two wines.
observations.chain: made all nations drink → God remembered Babylon → drain the cup (Rev 14:8; 16:19)
observations.parties: Babylon; the nations; the kings and merchants; God
observations.setting: the second and third angels, one after the other (Rev 14:8, 10); the lament over Babylon (18:3).
observations.meaning: thymos is Babylon's "passion" and God's "wrath", in consecutive verses, each in the phrase the wine of.
observations.implication: the verses set the two wines side by side themselves; the one who made the nations drink is made to drain the cup (16:19, AG-215). No anger in 14:8 or 18:3.

observations.text: "I will make you angry."
observations.parties: God; Moses; Paul; Israel; "a foolish nation"
observations.setting: Paul asks "did Israel not understand?" and answers with Moses (Rom 10:19, from Deu 32:21; unit 3 AG-126).
observations.meaning: God is the one who provokes, Israel the one made angry, jealousy beside the anger.
observations.implication: the answer-in-kind of Deu 32:21 (AG-126) carried into the Greek.

observations.text: Jesus looked around at them with anger.
observations.chain: asked, they were silent → looked with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart → "Stretch out your hand" → restored (3:4–5) · went out → counsel how to destroy him (3:6)
observations.parties: Jesus; the Pharisees and Herodians; the man with the withered hand
observations.meaning: the anger follows a question met with silence. It is joined with grief, and aimed at the hardness of their hearts. Jesus's next words are to the man: "Stretch out your hand". The other party's response is counsel to destroy him.

observations.text: Jesus indignant for the children.
observations.chain: saw it → indignant → "Let the children come to me" (10:14)
observations.parties: Jesus; the disciples; the children and those who brought them
observations.meaning: aganakteō, the word used of the disciples' indignation at waste and at rivals (5Q, 5R), is here Jesus's, at his disciples, for the children.
observations.implication: one word, aimed three ways (AN §L.2).

observations.text: The master's anger in the parables.
observations.chain: should have had mercy → in anger delivered to the jailers (Mat 18:33–34) → so also my heavenly Father, if you do not forgive from your heart (18:35) · killed his servants → the king angry → destroyed, burned (22:6–7) · made excuses → angry → bring in the poor (Luk 14:18–21)
observations.parties: the master, the king, the master of the house; the servant and his fellow servant; the invited; the poor, crippled, blind and lame; the Father
observations.setting: three of Jesus's parables: the unforgiving servant (Mat 18:23–35), the wedding feast (Mat 22:1–14), the great banquet (Luk 14:16–24).
observations.meaning: each master is angry at what was done with what he offered: mercy not passed on, an invitation refused and its messengers killed, excuses. Jesus applies the first to the Father and the heart. In Luke the anger issues in a wider invitation.
observations.implication: I read the three as anger at grace refused or not passed on; each verse states its own occasion.

observations.text: The devil's great wrath, because his time is short.
observations.chain: thrown down → come down in great wrath, because his time is short (Rev 12:12) · became furious with the woman → went off to make war on her offspring (Rev 12:17)
observations.parties: the devil, the dragon; the brothers; the woman and her offspring; the heavens; earth and sea
observations.setting: the war in heaven and its song (Rev 12:7–12), and the dragon's pursuit of the woman (12:13–17).
observations.meaning: the only hits in this unit where a spirit is the angry one. The reason is stated: he knows his time is short. His fury is aimed at those who keep God's commandments.
observations.implication: ruling 6.2: a spirit as the angry party, with a stated reason and a stated target. New for 10.13. Eph 4:27 (AG-223) names the devil as given opportunity by anger kept overnight; a pointer, not a join.

observations.text: Anger in the lists.
observations.parties: Paul; the readers; the Spirit; God in Christ
observations.setting: six lists in Paul's letters (Gal 5:19–23; Eph 4:31–32; Col 3:8; 2Cor 12:20; Rom 1:29; Rom 13:13).
observations.meaning: anger and strife stand among works of the flesh, among things to be put away, among what Paul fears to find at Corinth. Jealousy or envy stands beside them in 4 of the 6 lists (Rom 1:29; 2Cor 12:20; Gal 5:20–21; Rom 13:13). Words of the mouth (clamor, slander, obscene talk, gossip) stand beside them in 3 (Eph 4:31; Col 3:8; 2Cor 12:20). Three lists name what replaces them: the fruit of the Spirit; kindness and forgiving "as God in Christ forgave you"; walking "properly as in the daytime" (Rom 13:13).
observations.implication: in these lists anger is something a person is told to put off, and is named with its companions.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Gal 5:20; Eph 4:31; Col 3:8; Rom 1:29); W (2Cor 12:20; Rom 13:13); also appears: 12; 10.5; 14 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Be angry and do not sin.
observations.chain: do not let the sun go down on your anger, and give no opportunity to the devil (4:26–27)
observations.parties: the believer; the neighbour; the devil
observations.meaning: the anger itself is not forbidden; its length is limited (sunset). Five verses later the same chapter says "Let all … anger … be put away" (4:31). The words differ: orgizō and parorgismos in 4:26, orgē in 4:31.
observations.implication: the chapter holds both statements; I record them side by side, not reconciled.

observations.text: Slow to anger; man's anger and God's righteousness.
observations.chain: anger of man → does not produce the righteousness of God (1:20) → therefore put away … receive with meekness the implanted word (1:21)
observations.parties: James; the brothers; God
observations.meaning: hearing, speaking and anger in one sentence, with a speed for each. The reason given is what anger does not produce.

observations.text: Angry with a brother.
observations.chain: angry with his brother → liable to judgment (5:22) · remember your brother has something against you → leave your gift → first be reconciled (5:23–24)
observations.parties: Jesus; the brother; the one who offers
observations.meaning: AN-23. Already in 10.10.

observations.text: Without anger: in prayer, in the overseer, in love.
observations.parties: the men who pray; the overseer; love
observations.setting: Paul to Timothy on prayer (1Ti 2:8); to Titus on the overseer, "as God's steward" (Tit 1:7); on love (1Cor 13:4–5).
observations.meaning: anger is named by its absence: from hands lifted in prayer, from one who oversees, from love.
observations.implication: the hands in prayer touch OT-06.
observations.note: October disposition: D (1Ti 2:8; 1Cor 13:5); W (Tit 1:7); also appears: 10.4; 11; 10.1; 10.10 (1Ti 2:8; 1Cor 13:5); OT-06 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: When they heard: rage, the body, and killing.
observations.chain: heard → filled with wrath → drove him out, to throw him down (Luk 4:28–29) · heard → enraged → wanted to kill → Gamaliel's counsel (Act 5:33–35) · heard → enraged, ground their teeth → stopped their ears, rushed → stoned (Act 7:54–58) · heard → enraged → crying out → the city filled with confusion (Act 19:28–29)
observations.parties: the synagogue at Nazareth; the council, Gamaliel; Stephen's hearers, Stephen, Saul; Demetrius and the craftsmen; Jesus; the apostles; Paul
observations.setting: Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luk 4:16–30); the apostles before the council (Act 5:27–40); Stephen's speech (Act 7:54–58); Demetrius and the craftsmen (Act 19:24–29).
observations.meaning: in all four the verse says when they heard. The rage goes at once into the body: rising up, grinding teeth, stopping ears, rushing, crying out. In three of the four it moves to killing (Luk 4:29; Act 5:33; Act 7:58). In Ephesus the speaker names the trade at risk (19:27). In the council a Pharisee's counsel stops it (5:34–35).
observations.implication: extends AN-01 (anger kindled by something perceived) and AG-149 (God hears, unit 4). The stopped ears are hearing refused (10.2).
observations.note: October disposition: D (Act 7:54); W; also appears: 10.2 (Act 7:54) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Herod's fury.
observations.chain: tricked → furious → sent and killed (Mat 2:16) · angry → they persuaded Blastus → asked for peace, because their country depended on his for food (Act 12:20)
observations.parties: Herod the Great; the wise men; the children of Bethlehem; Herod Agrippa; Tyre and Sidon; Blastus; an angel of the Lord
observations.setting: Matthew 2; Act 12:20–23.
observations.meaning: the ruler's anger goes straight to a command (as AG-182). Those beneath it in Acts seek peace through the chamberlain, and the reason given is food. The same Herod is struck down because he did not give God the glory.
observations.implication: extends AG-182 (anger with power to command). Act 12:23 is held for OT-08.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Act 12:20); W; H (12:23); also appears: 10.10 (Act 12:20); 10.1 (Mat 2:16, AN-01) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Not afraid of the king's anger.
observations.chain: as seeing him who is invisible → not afraid of the anger of the king (11:27)
observations.parties: Moses; Pharaoh; "him who is invisible"
observations.meaning: AN-34. Already in 10.12.

observations.text: Indignant at waste.
observations.chain: saw it → indignant → "Why this waste?" (Mat 26:8) → Jesus: "she has done a beautiful thing" (26:10)
observations.parties: the disciples; "some"; the woman; Jesus; the poor
observations.setting: the anointing at Bethany (Mat 26:6–13; Mar 14:3–9).
observations.meaning: the indignation has a reason that sounds right (the poor). In Mark it is said to themselves: the indignation is first inward speech. Jesus answers by naming what the woman has done.
observations.implication: extends AN §L.3 whether it is seen truly.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Mat 26:8); W (Mar 14:4); also appears: 10.1 (Mat 26:8) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Indignant at rivals.
observations.chain: heard → indignant at the two → Jesus called them → whoever would be great must be your servant (Mat 20:24–26)
observations.parties: the ten; James and John; Jesus
observations.setting: after the mother of James and John asks for places beside Jesus (Mat 20:20–28; Mar 10:35–45).
observations.meaning: the ten are indignant at the two for seeking the first place. Jesus does not rebuke the indignation; he calls all twelve and names what greatness is among them.
observations.implication: the answer the anger meets is a teaching on serving (AN §L.3, the answer it meets).

observations.text: Indignant at healing, praise and teaching.
observations.chain: healed on the Sabbath → indignant → spoke to the people (Luk 13:14) → Jesus's answer → adversaries put to shame, people rejoiced (13:15–17) · teaching the resurrection → greatly annoyed → arrested (Act 4:2–3)
observations.parties: the ruler of the synagogue; the woman bound by Satan; the crowd; the chief priests and scribes; the children; the priests, the captain, the Sadducees; Peter and John; Jesus
observations.meaning: the occasion each time is something done for people (a healing, praise, teaching), and the indignant are those with religious charge. Jesus answers with their own practice (the ox led to water; circumcision on the Sabbath) or their own scripture. In Luke the answer puts his adversaries to shame and the people rejoice (13:17). In Acts the annoyance moves to arrest. diaponeomai, "greatly annoyed", is the priests' word here and Paul's at the spirit of divination (AG-234).
observations.implication: extends AN §L.3 for what.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Luk 13:14); W; also appears: 10.8 (Luk 13:14) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The older brother.
observations.chain: heard → angry → refused to go in → father came out and entreated (15:27–28)
observations.parties: the older son; the father; the younger son; the servant
observations.meaning: the anger follows what he heard from a servant (15:26–27) and keeps him outside. He speaks of this son of yours; the father answers this your brother. The father comes out and entreats. The parable ends on the father's words; the son's answer is not told.
observations.implication: the answer the anger meets (AN §L.3) is the father's going out and his words. "Was dead, and is alive" is held (OT-08).
observations.note: October disposition: W; H (15:32); also appears: 10.4 (AN-16) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Paul's spirit provoked; greatly annoyed.
observations.chain: his spirit provoked as he saw idols → so he reasoned (17:16–17) · kept doing this many days → greatly annoyed → commanded the spirit → it came out (16:18)
observations.parties: Paul; the city's idols; the slave girl; the spirit of divination; her owners
observations.setting: Athens (Act 17:16–17); Philippi, the slave girl with a spirit of divination who cried out "These men are servants of the Most High God" (16:16–18).
observations.meaning: paroxynō is seated in Paul's spirit and follows what he saw; it leads to daily reasoning. diaponeomai comes after many days, and Paul speaks to the spirit, not to the girl.
observations.implication: ruling 6.2: a spirit is the party Paul's annoyance is aimed at. The provoking word is also love's not irritable (1Cor 13:5) and the sharp disagreement (Act 15:39) (§C).
observations.note: October disposition: D (17:16); W (16:18); also appears: 10.1; 06; 10.9 (Act 17:16) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Indignation produced by godly grief.
observations.chain: godly grief → repentance → salvation; worldly grief → death (7:10) · godly grief → produced earnestness, eagerness, indignation, fear, longing, zeal (7:11)
observations.parties: Paul; the Corinthians; his letter
observations.setting: Paul on the effect of his severe letter (2Cor 7:8–11).
observations.meaning: indignation is named among what godly grief produced, beside fear, longing and zeal; aimed, I read, at the wrong they had allowed.
observations.implication: cross-cluster association: grief (M03) and fear (M01) stand with indignation in one verse (§F). "Worldly grief produces death" is held (OT-08).
observations.note: October disposition: D; H (7:10); also appears: 10.1; 14; M03; OT-08 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Fighting without, fear within.
observations.parties: Paul and his companions; God; Titus
observations.meaning: machē here is conflict borne from outside, beside fear inside, and the body without rest. The comfort comes from God through a person.

observations.text: Where strife comes from.
observations.chain: passions at war within → quarrels and fights (Jam 4:1) · covet, cannot obtain → fight and quarrel (4:2) · jealousy and strife → of the flesh (1Cor 3:3) · conceit, craving → quarrels about words → envy, dissension, slander (1Ti 6:4) · controversies → breed quarrels (2Ti 2:23)
observations.parties: believers; the conceited; those who cause divisions; Chloe's people; Paul; James
observations.setting: James; 1 Corinthians (reported "by Chloe's people", 1:11); the letters to Timothy and Titus; Galatians; Philippians; Romans.
observations.meaning: the strife is among believers, and its source is named inside the person: passions at war, coveting, jealousy, the flesh, conceit, a craving. Not asking God is named beside the coveting (Jam 4:2). Strife also breeds more: quarrels about words produce envy, dissension, slander. The answer given is to avoid: the controversies, the divisive.
observations.implication: extends unit 4 AG-191 (strife between people: where it comes from, what ends it) into the church.
observations.note: October disposition: D (Jam 4:1); W; also appears: 12; 10.10; 10.6 (Jam 4:1) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: The sharp disagreement.
observations.chain: Paul thought best not → sharp disagreement → separated (Act 15:38–39)
observations.parties: Paul; Barnabas; Mark; Silas; the brothers
observations.setting: Act 15:36–41, as the second journey begins.
observations.meaning: two workers, each with a reason stated; the outcome is separation, and both go on working. The verse gives no verdict on who was right.
observations.implication: paroxysmos, the word used here, is also stir up one another to love (Heb 10:24, AG-239).

observations.text: Provoke: to anger, or to love.
observations.chain: provoke your children → lest they become discouraged (Col 3:21) · your zeal → stirred up most of them (2Cor 9:2)
observations.parties: fathers; children; believers; the Corinthians; the Macedonians
observations.setting: the household codes (Eph 6:4; Col 3:21); Hebrews on meeting together (Heb 10:24–25); Paul on the Corinthians' readiness to give (2Cor 9:2).
observations.meaning: one party can provoke another's anger. Colossians gives what it leads to: discouragement. The same two roots (erethizō, paroxysmos) are used for stirring others to love, good works and giving.
observations.implication: what the stirring is aimed at decides what it is (AN §L.2, AN §L.3). Cross-cluster association: discouragement (§F).
observations.note: October disposition: D (Col 3:21; Heb 10:24); W (Eph 6:4; 2Cor 9:2); also appears: 10.1; 10.10; 11; 14; 15 (Col 3:21; Heb 10:24) (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)

observations.text: Hot and cold.
observations.chain: lukewarm → I will spit you out (3:16) · those whom I love, I reprove → be zealous and repent (3:19)
observations.parties: the one who speaks; the church in Laodicea
observations.setting: the letter to Laodicea (Rev 3:14–22), which says "I am rich … I need nothing" (3:17).
observations.meaning: zestos is the heat of works, not anger. The call that follows is to zeal and repentance.
observations.implication: a heat word with no anger in it (OT-15, the heat family). Data for this strand; a cross-cluster association with zeal (§F).
observations.note: October disposition: data; also appears: OT-15 (_analytics/Clusters/M02 - anger-wrath/anger-observation-ledger-unit5-v1-20261005.md)
